name: The Charred Note at Waluigi's Door
title: The Charred Note at Waluigi's Door, and What It Claimed About Mario After the Farm
type: Recovered Note / Alleged Confession / Mario Disappearance Evidence
status: Filed as contested evidence — no part of the note accepted without corroboration
summary: Before dawn, a smoke-scented note appeared outside Waluigi's borrowed room at Tymnas's cottage. It was burned neatly around the edges and titled SECRET HISTORY MARIO. The text claims Mario admitted that Peach died by his hand, that the eastern farm lasted three days rather than years, that he died there and woke up afterward, that he once belonged to the Mages' Guild, and that three null cages failed against him without any visible counterspell. Waluigi does not believe a theatrical unsigned confession merely because it was dramatic. Waluigi files it anyway, because forged evidence is still evidence of what someone wants the archive to think about.
description:
Waluigi opened the door before sunrise and found the page exactly where a person would leave something meant to be discovered and exactly where the wind would never have managed to slide it on its own. The planks outside Tymnas's borrowed rooms still held the night's damp. The hedge beyond them was beaded with the last of the mist. Somewhere farther out, where the maze gave way to the darker line of the hanging grounds, a bird made one irritated noise and then thought better of participating in the morning.

The paper did not belong to that hour. It smelled of smoke, not of hearth smoke or camp smoke or the broad, ordinary smell of a cottage that had survived too many magical problems in too few days. This was sharper than that. Cooked edges. Dry ash. A document that had been brought close enough to flame to be transformed and then removed before the sentence in the middle could be touched. The burn line ran inward from three sides, controlled and even enough to offend Waluigi on sight. Accidents are messy. This was layout.

The title was still perfectly legible: [[prop:prop_charred_note_secret_history_mario|SECRET HISTORY MARIO]].

He did not kick it first, though he considered it. He crouched instead, two fingers on one corner, and lifted it the way one lifts a dead insect off a good coat. The ash held where it was. Nothing sloughed away. The fold remained crisp. No rain had got to it. No dew had touched it. Whoever put it there had not merely left a note. Whoever put it there had staged its entrance.

Waluigi filed the physical condition separately as a [[prop:prop_charred_note_custody_slip|threshold custody slip]], because the burn pattern mattered almost as much as the words. Somebody had not failed to destroy this page. Somebody had wanted the archive to watch them pretend.

## Part One:


The Threshold, the Table, and the Fact of Audience

He took the page inside and shut the door with his heel. The cottage was not warm yet. Last night's heat had thinned to a smell of old wood and tired ash in the grate. The table near the wall still held the ordinary wreckage of people surviving a campaign badly: a cup with a brown ring in the bottom, crumbs worked into the grain, a bent spoon, thread, one dead moth by the sill. Waluigi set the page down beside the cup and looked at it again from standing height, because sometimes a stupid object improves when forced to share a table with real ones.

This one improved in exactly the wrong direction.

From above, the burn looked even more deliberate. The paper had been sacrificed around the center as if the center were a stage actor and the rest of the page had agreed to die for lighting. The title line sat untouched. The body beneath it had been spared with almost insulting precision. Waluigi touched the edge with one nail and came away with a gray smear. Fresh enough to mark. Old enough not to crumble. Somebody had timed this.

*WAH! Anonymous documents always imagine they are clever because they arrive uninvited. A document is not clever merely because it knows what a doorway is. It becomes clever only if the person reading it wishes it did not exist, and this one cleared that bar immediately.*

What bothered him first was not the name in the title. It was the audience assumption. This page had not been left in a common room for anybody to find. It had not been pinned to the wall, weighed under a mug, tucked under a plate, or hidden where chance discovery could plausibly explain itself. It had been put outside **his** door. That meant whoever placed it knew which room was Waluigi's, knew he would be awake before most of the cottage, and knew—correctly—that he would pick it up rather than burn it unread out of spite.

That is not a broad delivery. That is a tailored one.

He unfolded it fully and read the opening lines once without sitting down, because first readings are for impact and second readings are for embarrassment. The page attempted impact at once. Mario, in the body of the note, was not introduced as missing or mourned or misunderstood. He was introduced as a threat. The staged scene had him breathing smoke, grinding a cigar into stone, demanding answers from an unnamed questioner like a tyrant who had already decided he disliked the room. Bowser's name was there. Luigi's name was there. The writer had not bothered with a soft entrance. The writer knew what file this page wanted to invade and had walked in swinging.

Waluigi sat.

The chair made a little wood complaint under him. He flattened the page with both palms and started over, slower.

## Part Two:


The Voice on the Page

The body reads like a transcript somebody wanted mistaken for revelation.

That distinction matters. A genuine transcript preserves hesitation whether it wants to or not. It leaves in the repetition, the badly timed question, the answer that arrives at the wrong angle, the detail nobody would think to invent because it is too small to feel worth the trouble. A staged transcript knows where the spotlight is. It enters each revelation one step too cleanly. This page knew its spotlights.

The unnamed speaker presses Mario in exactly the order most damaging to the existing file: Peach first, because she is the oldest wound; the eastern disappearance second, because the archive is already unstable there; the Mages' Guild third, because institutions make excellent accelerants; the Star Fountain last, because by then the reader is already off balance and much easier to tip.

That alone would make Waluigi suspicious. The page then makes the mistake of being **too** efficient. Each new pressure point produces not confusion but escalation. Mention Peach and Mario does not deny the death. Mention grief and he does not retreat to the easier explanation. He leaps forward to the ugliest possible one. Question the farm and the page does not merely correct the old timeline. It replaces it. Raise the Guild and the paper rewards itself with a procedural catastrophe. Everything sharpens when touched. Real people dull in places. This page had no dull spots at all.

And yet the writer had done enough homework to be dangerous.

The note understood Mario's archive presence as it currently exists: not just a vanished hero, but a vanished hero already surrounded by contradictory filings. It knew Luigi had confessed to a farm. It knew the Star Fountain mattered more than Waluigi had been able to prove. It knew Peach sits behind all of it whether anyone likes that or not. It knew the Guild's name carries more weight if attached not to a contract or a badge but to a failure of containment. Whoever wrote this had not assembled rumor from across a tavern. Whoever wrote this had either read the file or had been briefed by someone who had.

That narrows the sender more than any ash sample ever will.

The opening posture also does a particular kind of work Waluigi resents on principle: it makes Mario competent at menace in exactly the way a nervous audience expects him to be. Cold eyes. slow step. measured threat. smoke from the nostrils. Not because the archive has ever proved any of that presentation, but because the writer knows that an audience primed by disappearance, tyranny rumors, and old war stories will accept stage villainy as historical texture if the page feeds it enough atmosphere quickly enough.

The atmosphere is bait.

Waluigi kept reading anyway.

## Part Three:


The Peach Claim

The note's first major claim is the line no reader is supposed to recover from quickly:

> "I didn't leave because of grief."
>
> "I left because I killed her."

Waluigi read it once, then again, then once more not because repetition made it more believable but because disbelief is not the same as immunity. A forged confession can still land like a hammer if it names the right stone.

Why this line is targeted is obvious. The Mario file already runs backward through Princess Peach whether the archive wants it to or not. Every route out of the disappearance eventually trips over the assassination question, the Regency question, Bowser's official blame, the Loyalists' counter-narrative, and the possibility that eighty-five years of Mushroom Kingdom history were built on a lie tidy enough to govern with. The page knows all this. Instead of arguing about arrangements, conspiracies, forged journals, or disputed witnesses, it simply drops Mario himself into the center of the crime and dares the archive to cope.

It is an efficient cruelty. It takes a sprawling historical wound and reduces it to a single mouth saying *I did it.*

That is exactly why Waluigi refuses to accept it on style alone.

The page gives itself supporting theatre, naturally. A locket appears. Peach's younger face on one side. Mario on the other. A wedding image with Bowser as witness, because the writer understands perfectly that the archive has room for one more contradiction but not for a boring one. If the locket had shown a registry office and two anonymous clerks, the note would be weaker. So Bowser is put there grinning in the memory-space, because outrageous details adhere in the mind longer than plausible ones.

*Waluigi notes for the record that outrageous details are not self-proving. They are only sticky. Syrup is sticky too. That does not make breakfast a legal document.*

The note then doubles down by refusing the ordinary emotional reading. Mario does not melt. He does not confess out of guilt. He does not collapse into remorse. He grows colder and more disgusted, as though even the suggestion of grief insults him. This is dramatically effective and evidentially suspicious. A page this interested in controlling audience response will always choose disgust over sorrow if it wants the reader to continue. Sorrow closes scenes. Disgust keeps them moving.

Still, the line cannot simply be discarded, because even if false it announces intent with almost obscene clarity. Someone wants Peach moved from historical background radiation to immediate active cause. Someone wants the reader to stop asking whether Peach's death drove Mario away and start asking whether Peach's death was the thing Mario carried east with him because he caused it. That is not a neutral change in emphasis. It is a rerouting.

Waluigi files reroutings.

## Part Four:


The Farm Story Before the Rewrite

Before this page arrived, the farm was already a problem.

The archive's earlier eastern-passage file assembled merchant testimony, journal fragments, and a death record into a story that wanted badly to be true and could not survive arithmetic. The version Luigi had put into motion through the embassy confession gave Waluigi a direction, a rural hiding place, and a vanished brother who might have been alive longer than anyone expected. The eastern-passage file then made that direction worse by finding papers that described years on a farm after a Star Fountain reunion whose date left no years available. The contradiction was not subtle. It sat in the middle of the file like a wagon in a doorway.

This new note does not solve that contradiction honestly. It solves it by replacing the story.

Instead of years, the farm now lasts three days.

That change is not a small correction. It is the difference between exile and interruption. Years on a farm imply a chosen life, however peaceful or fabricated: labor, repetition, adaptation, the slow settling of a body into place. Three days imply barely enough time to become visible to a household before something ends. Three days make the farm not a second life but a station on the road to something else. Three days take the old story's calm and smash it with one phrase.

The note is explicit about the argument. When the questioner says reports mentioned months, Mario says no. When the page lets him describe the farm, it does so with suspiciously good pastoral detail—the tomatoes, the old couple, the dog, the dirt that smelled good, the work gloves, the morning harvest. Then, exactly when the reader is likely to begin treating this as corroboration of the old disappearance story, the page cuts the scene off with correction: three days, not months, not years, not some long pastoral retirement the archive can shelve neatly under tragedy.

In other words, the note uses the old farm story as cover long enough to kill it.

That is a move worth noticing no matter what one believes about Mario.

If the writer wanted to confirm Luigi's confession, they could have done so easily. They could have allowed the farm to remain long, lonely, and chronologically impossible. They did not. They instead targeted the exact weakness in the previous file and produced a new version designed to patch that weakness while opening a worse breach underneath it.

This is one of the reasons Waluigi is certain the sender understood the archive and was not improvising from rumor. A random liar repeats the public shape of a story. A useful liar corrects the contradiction inside it.

## Part Five: Death at the Farm, Waking Afterward


The page's next claim is the one that turns a timeline headache into an ontological one.

Asked what happened after the farm death, Mario says only: *I woke up.*

Waluigi hates how effective the sentence is.

It is effective because it is small. A longer explanation would have shown its joints. Resurrection by bargain, curse, machine, Star fragment, fungal contamination, planar slip, curse transfer, ghost occupancy, divine insult—there are half a dozen lurid ways this archive could be asked to swallow a return from death, and every one of them would immediately force the page to show its scaffolding. Instead, the note picks the shortest possible phrase and lets the reader drag their own fears into it.

That is good writing. It is also suspicious writing.

The page compounds the effect by placing this line after the three-day correction. If the farm had remained a place of years, *I woke up* might read as spiritual metaphor or memory fracture or a tired man's way of describing recovery from a breakdown. After the three-day version, with death made immediate, the same phrase becomes literal by pressure. The note knows this. The note is sequencing the reader.

And still Waluigi cannot dismiss the claim purely because it is sequenced well, because the file it attacks was already unable to explain itself. The eastern passage had a death record that behaved like it came from a future the calendar had not reached. This note, by collapsing the timeline, makes room for a death now—only not the peaceful death the earlier papers described. A person can read that as contradiction. A person can also read it as evidence that different hands have been trying to tell the archive incompatible versions of the same underlying event.

That possibility is worse than a simple forgery, because incompatible forgeries imply multiple interested parties, not one bored prankster with a candle.

What matters for the event filing is not that resurrection is now proven. It is not. What matters is that the archive has now received a piece of evidence explicitly designed to move the discussion from *where did Mario live?* to *what version of Mario existed after the farm?*

That is a wholly different question.

*WAH! This is the sort of development that makes a historian long for ordinary tax fraud. A dead hero who may have come back wrong is catastrophic. A dead hero who may have come back wrong **and** acquired paperwork problems is somehow worse.*

The page also uses death to recast cowardice. The questioner accuses Mario of running, hiding, staying gone, abandoning everyone for years. The reply in the note is not bravery exactly, but technical objection: *I wasn't hiding. I was dead.* It is the kind of answer a dramatist loves because it punishes the accusation while preserving menace. It is also exactly the answer one writes if one wants every prior witness who described disappearance to look merely incomplete rather than wholly false.

Again: replacement, not confirmation.

## Part Six:


The Mages' Guild Clause

The Guild enters the note with bluntness that would be comic if it were not so intentional.

The questioner asks whether Mario was a member. The data packet on his name, they say, comes up null except for a guild exception. Mario answers yes. No evasion. No qualification. Then the note immediately escalates to enforcement language: Section 1.6 of the C.C.D., rogue member, sanctioned duty, null cage, arrest.

Waluigi stopped there the first time through and put one thumb against his own eyebrow hard enough to hurt, because this is the point where the page stops being merely scandalous and becomes procedural.

Institutions are vulnerable to confident imitation. Most fabricated documents fail because the liar wants myth and the institution wants form. This note, however, knows enough form to be troublesome. It does not simply say *the Guild tried to stop him.* It specifies a section number. It invokes a codex. It names the tool of arrest. It has Mario recognize the Guild not as ambient background but as an old membership he personally admits.

If false, this is a very informed falsehood.

If true, the archive has been underestimating Mario in an entirely different direction.

The earlier files already brushed the Guild from several angles. Luigi is contract-bound to it. The arrangement file drags it toward Peach's assassination by allegation if not yet by proof. Historical Mages' Guild presences stain other arc records all over the archive. But those were institutional connections around Mario. This page tries to put the institution **inside** him: former member, still procedurally legible, still subject to codified arrest under a clause old enough to produce numbers.

That matters because former membership explains more than one anomaly at once if one lets it. It explains why the note bothers with null cages at all. It explains why Guild language is used not just decoratively but adversarially. It explains why the sender thought Guild procedure would be a meaningful pressure point in a Mario file that otherwise could have remained purely emotional.

Waluigi does not yet let it explain anything conclusively. But he is now forced to ask whether the archive's Mario dossier has been treating the Guild as adjacent when it might have been central all along.

And then the page does what it came to do.

## Part Seven:


The Three Null Cages

The arrest attempt is the core of the note whether the writer meant it to be or not.

Three null cages. Three impacts. Three failures.

The first cage does not close. It snaps in half. The note's internal explanation is not counterspell but rejection: the code itself refusing enforcement, or reality refusing to let Guild arrest bite on Mario. The second cage is met with laughter and explodes on contact. The third unravels quietly, almost politely, because by then the page no longer needs violence to make its point. The point has already been made twice. The third failure is ornament on the argument.

This sequence is shaped with theatrical intelligence. Three is the number at which pattern becomes myth in a reader's head. One failure is error. Two is complication. Three is a law of nature. A forger knows this the way a stage magician knows when to pause before opening the hand.

That does not mean Waluigi can file it as mere theatre and move on.

What gives the sequence force is not only repetition but the way the note frames comparison. The questioner mentions another mage once captured with such a cage. Mario is then measured against precedent and found more alarming, not less. The paper is telling the reader explicitly how to rank the event: not as generic magical resistance, but as procedural failure beyond the expected ceiling. Even if fabricated, that choice reveals the sender's goal. They do not merely want Mario feared. They want him feared in a way specific to Guild authority: beyond containment, beyond bureaucratic expectation, beyond the legal technology intended to reduce rogue members to manageable record lines.

That is a very institutional nightmare.

It also rewrites the significance of the farm death yet again. If the farm is where Mario died, and if the cages fail only afterward, then the note is not content with saying he survived something impossible. It is saying the impossible changed his relationship to systems built to classify him. Death, on this page, is not only event. It is jurisdictional breakage.

*Waluigi would like the world to stop producing problems whose legal implications are more terrifying than the corpse count. This request has not historically been granted.*

There is another reason the cages matter more than the confession line. A confession can always be planted in the mouth of a man the reader cannot presently interrogate. A failed procedure, especially a named one, invites external checking. Did such a clause exist? Did such arrests occur? Did any report go missing? Did any Guild file produce a dead stop around Mario's name except for an exception marker? Procedures leave paper when they fail. That makes this section of the note more dangerous to the sender than the Peach line if the sender is bluffing.

People lie most confidently where they expect nobody to verify. This note lies—if it is lying—about the part most likely to trigger verification work. That is bold. It is also odd.

Waluigi wrote that down before he reached the end of the page.

## Part Eight:


The Star Fountain Nod

The note saves the Star Fountain for last because the writer understands rhythm.

By the time the page reaches the fountain, the reader has already been dragged through Peach, the farm, death, waking, Guild membership, arrest authority, and three broken cages. The final question then arrives not as a new topic but as the locking pin through the whole arrangement: was the Star Meeting at the Fountain true, and did it happen with Luigi?

Mario's answer in the note is not a speech. It is a nod.

That choice is irritatingly effective. Speeches can be argued with. Nods feel like admission stripped of decoration, and admission stripped of decoration feels more authentic than it often is. The note knows this. It has already overperformed elsewhere. Here, restraint costs less and buys more.

The earlier fountain file already suffered from too many versions at once: who arrived first, whether a third figure existed, what was said, where they flew, what the activation meant, whether the witnesses were lying, whether the geography matched the chronology. The new note does not repair any of those questions. It merely asserts the event happened and uses that assertion as a terminal note of agreement between the page and the archive's prior hunger.

That is why Waluigi refuses to call it closure.

A final nod does not settle the order of witnesses, the question of the third presence, the route out, or the meaning of Luigi's subsequent silence. It only tells the file that the writer knew the fountain was the one point the archive most wanted affirmed. The affirmation therefore carries less independent weight than a naive reader might think. It is not neutral evidence. It is selected comfort—or selected discomfort—provided precisely where it will echo longest.

And yet even selected comfort is informative. The writer did not choose to deny the fountain. The writer chose to ratify it. This tells the file that whoever is trying to control the Mario narrative now considers the fountain load-bearing enough to preserve while replacing almost everything else around it.

That is a strategic decision.

The fountain stays. The years go. The peaceful death goes. The postwar drift goes. In their place: three days, one death, one waking, one Guild breakage.

A person can learn a great deal from what a liar leaves untouched.

## Part Nine: Delivery Method, Sender Profile, and the Reason the


Ash Matters

Once he reached the bottom of the page, Waluigi did not set it aside at once. He looked back at the burn before reading the first line again, because by then the physical object and the narrative object had fused into the same problem.

The delivery method matters because it is the sender's one unavoidable confession. Even if every word inside the note was fabricated, the note still had to arrive somehow. Someone knew the room. Someone chose the hour. Someone either walked the threshold or had access to a route that let the paper appear there without broad notice. Someone was confident enough that Waluigi would read rather than destroy. Someone also understood that a plain unburned page would have been filed as message, whereas a charred page invites the reader to imagine survival, suppression, rescue, theft from a fire, evidence dragged back from deliberate destruction.

The sender wanted all those associations for free.

That is why the ash matters. Not because ash proves truth, but because ash is argument.

The threshold slip records what the eye told him at once: no envelope, no seal, no footprint, no water damage, ash inward rather than scattered. The burn line is even. The title survives too neatly. The fold remained clean. The note was not discovered after catastrophe. It was manufactured to resemble discovery after catastrophe.

This makes the sender neither omnipotent nor subtle. It makes them theatrical, targeted, and familiar with Waluigi's weaknesses. Vanity, curiosity, suspicion, inability to leave a bad mystery alone—these are all exploitable traits in an archivist. Waluigi records that without pleasure because it is true. The sender built the note to catch exactly those hooks, and the hooks worked because here the page is, filed permanently.

Still, the sender's success does not invalidate the archive's response. The correct answer to targeted evidence is not to ignore it. The correct answer is to file the targeting as part of the evidence and proceed with contempt sharpened into method.

This is now method.

## Part Ten: What Changed the Morning This Was Filed


Before the note, the Mario disappearance file was unstable in one way. After the note, it is unstable in three.

First: the temporal problem changed shape. The eastern passage had too many years inside too little time. The charred note eliminates the years. That does not solve the archive's difficulty. It creates a replacement narrative in which the contradiction is no longer about chronology but about what happened after death.

Second: the institutional problem sharpened. The Guild is no longer merely adjacent through Luigi, rumors, or historical accusations. The note attempts to place Mario himself inside Guild procedure and then outside it again, as a former member upon whom Section 1.6 can be invoked and against whom null cages fail. If this is fabricated, the fabrication is highly educated. If it is true, the archive is late to a very ugly party.

Third: the fountain has been promoted. What was once a contested reunion with too many witness problems now becomes, in this note's architecture, the one fixed hinge the replacement narrative chooses to keep. That means every future reading of the Star Fountain has to account for the possibility that hostile or manipulative hands consider it indispensable.

Waluigi hates all three developments. He hates them more because none is yet dispositive. There is no clean verdict to issue this morning. Only movement.

The page therefore enters the archive under the only description honest enough to survive a second reading: contested evidence with targeted intent.

Waluigi has opened a new investigation because the archive no longer has the luxury of pretending the farm story is the same story it was yesterday. If the farm lasted three days, and if the death there was real, and if the waking afterward changed what Guild procedure can touch, then the question is no longer *where did Mario go after the fountain?* The question is *what came back from the farm, who wants that version of the story installed, and why did they decide Waluigi needed to read it before breakfast?*

That is now the file.

Waluigi hates that this is now a serious question.

Waluigi hates it enough to keep going.

description:
Waluigi is going to open with the sentence that decides this filing, because everything after it is consequence.

**A man picked up a wounded Toad and walked off with him, and he was right by his own rules and wrong by everybody else's, and no two people in that grove agreed about which mattered.**
outcome: The Scorncrow is dead and the party is in a worse position than before it died. An Iron Legion guard took the unconscious Salam on his shoulder and left against the objections of Archie, Feyward Dan and Markop, citing the Legion code — no man left behind — and stating plainly that he trusts himself more than them and will not leave a casualty with the people who produced one. The promised helicopter never arrived; the guards left on foot, fireman-carrying Salam after one of them tripped and Salam was briefly dragged by a spider. Archie erased the crossed-out lines in his spellbook, circled his last high-level spell, and cast Fireball at a bush, setting the grove alight for the second time in two filings with the party still inside it. Markop stopped his own bleeding, was surrounded, stepped on spider eggs mid-declaration, and was extracted by Dan's javelin and a barrier cast across the grove before he threw it; he ended the night sitting on Wario's motorbike with no idea how to ride it. Remi stripped her destroyed dress, took a chain shirt and a battle axe off a body, healed herself twice without getting right, and walked out of the grove under her own power — then ran into a room of wrights with Wario and Mossy. Pierce Anamatar offered passage out of Guild-controlled ground in exchange for a possession, asked for the siglet, declined an expired coupon, and accepted Remi's Gehenna Academy student ID because it is durable. The three Toads were left in the dirt watching everyone else leave.

aftermath:
**The grove is burning again.** Archie lit it with his last high-level spell, aimed at a bush, with everyone still inside.

**The party is in four pieces.** Markop is on a motorbike he cannot ride. Feyward Dan and Eager are surrounded. Remi, Wario and Mossy are in Anamatar's den with passage bought. The three Toads are in the dirt watching everyone leave.

**The Legion has Salam.** Salam left in a fireman's carry, bound for Legionhold — the same facility the guards promised would host Archie's arrest.

**No helicopter came.** It was promised twice and never appeared.

**Remi has no student ID.** Pierce Anamatar has it, and it is the last document proving she was ever enrolled at Gehenna Academy.

**Unresolved:** what Anamatar wants with a student card; whether the Legion will return Salam; and whether anyone told the three Toads what happened.
waluigiAssessment:
**The argument over Eager is the filing and the fire is the punchline.**

Waluigi has read the exchange between Markop and the guard a dozen times looking for the party's side to be obviously right, and it is not. The guard said he would not leave half a dead person with people who gallivant around and get killed, and he said it standing over a grove containing one fallen Toad, one man fighting while badly hurt, and a Toad unconscious on his shoulder. **The evidence was on his side.** He was rude, he was unilateral, and he was not wrong.

What makes it a dispute rather than a rescue is the second half of his sentence: *I trust myself more than you guys.* That is not the code talking. The code was the justification he reached for; the distrust was the reason. And Eager — awake enough to ask — told him to put him down, and he did not.

**Then Archie set the grove on fire.** Waluigi wants to be careful here, because Markop had just shouted for exactly that and the spiders were closing. But the sequence in the record is: erase the crossed-out lines, find the last high-level spell, circle it, aim at a **bush**. One spell of that grade left in the book, spent on shrubbery, in a grove that was already burned once, while nine people were standing in it.

Everybody who was surrounded before the fireball was still surrounded after it. The only thing that changed is that the room is now on fire.

**And then there is the card.**

Pierce Anamatar could have asked for gold. He asked for a possession, twice now — a contract paid in passage home on a rooftop, and tonight a piece of laminate belonging to a fourteen-year-old. He declined an expired coupon, which means he was choosing, not taking whatever was offered.

Remi left Gehenna Academy without a formal withdrawal. That card was the only document in the world still asserting she had been a student somewhere. She traded it to get three people out of a burning wood, and she did it without visible hesitation, and Waluigi does not think she has worked out yet what she handed over.

**What the night actually cost:** a promised helicopter that never came, a wizard's last big spell spent on a bush, Salam in Legion custody, a paladin surrounded, a centaur on a motorbike he cannot ride, three Toads abandoned in the dirt, and a girl's name coming off the only paper that carried it.

They killed the Scorncrow last filing. Waluigi would like somebody to explain what they won.

WAH.

sections.name: I. The Guard, the Code, and the Argument Nobody Won
sections.overview:
An [Iron Legion](#/article/iron_legion) guard hoisted [Salam](#/article/salam) onto his shoulder. *I'll take him to safety.* An Iron Legion hospital, he said. The best one in the area, he said later, to Markop, as though the quality of the ward were the objection.

[Archie](#/article/archie_miser) said no. [Feyward Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) ran over and asked what he was doing. [Markop](#/article/markop) told him he was not part of the group and had no standing to take one of theirs.

The guard's answer was procedural and, Waluigi concedes, internally consistent: *I can't drop him. It's part of the Legion code. No man left behind.* When Salam himself said please, drop our friend, the guard did not.

Then the real argument surfaced, and it was not about the code at all:

> *I'm not leaving half a dead person here while you guys gallivant around and get killed. I trust myself more than you guys.*

Markop's counter was the only one available — he is part of our squad, once this is over we patch him up, don't take one of our guys away from us. The guard's reply was the line Waluigi keeps returning to: **your incompetence is beyond me.** Markop said: we killed the Scorncrow. The guard said: *you may have killed him, but look at what cost.*

Waluigi has read that exchange several times looking for the side that is wrong and cannot find one. [Salam](#/article/salam) is face-down. Markop is badly hurt but still fighting. Eager is unconscious. The guard looked at that and declined to leave a casualty with the people who produced it. That is not cowardice. It is an assessment, and it is not obviously incorrect.
sections.waluigi_note: An Iron Legion guard hoisting a casualty onto his shoulder and offering an evacuation hospital that doesn't exist. Waluigi records the military bedside manner.

sections.name: II. A Helicopter, and a Toad Who Has Never Heard of One
sections.overview:
*Not to worry — we have a helicopter to airlift us all out of here.*

**"What's a helicopter?"** said Dan.

Waluigi wants that preserved exactly. A Toad paladin from a plane with no sky, standing in a burning web, being promised evacuation by a machine he has no word for. The guards went further: they would put on quite a show, and Archie would be taken away to *Legionhold*, their very own.

Dan's response to the promise of arrest for his colleague was *no matter that*, and then he smote an ettercap with his longsword and went to notify everyone else.

**No helicopter arrived.** Nothing in the record shows one. The guards left on foot, carrying Salam in a fireman's carry, at a sprint.
sections.waluigi_note: Dan asking 'What's a helicopter?' while standing in burning ash. A paladin who understands planar rifts and holy smites completely baffled by rotary aviation.

sections.name: III. Remi, Alone, Doing the Arithmetic
sections.overview:
[Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) had a moment to herself and used it like a professional.

She checked the blood — *where did this come from* — which is the correct first question and one nobody else asked all night. Her dress was already destroyed by the hooks. She took it off, and pulled a **chain shirt** off a body, and put that on instead. She picked up a shield, looked at it, and left it for now.

Then she healed herself. It was not enough. She did it again. *Okay, now I'm feeling a little bit... still not enough.*

She took a **battle axe** off the same body. Then she walked out of the grove and escaped, which is the only clean exit anybody managed under their own power.

Waluigi notes the sequence — assess, re-armour, self-treat, re-arm, leave — and notes that four filings ago she was hiding behind Markop.
sections.waluigi_note: Checking the blood on her sleeve, counting remaining supplies, and preparing an exit route before the fire consumes the branches. Professional triage under fire.

sections.name: IV. Markop, Surrounded
sections.overview:
Three spiders in front of him. One giant green one and two smaller behind. Closing.

He stopped his own bleeding first — he is no longer bloody, which the archive records because he had been fighting already badly hurt from the execution. Then he called to Archie: **use fireball, use your lightning, anything, before they close in.**

Eager swung at a spider, missed, and hit the guard carrying Salam.

Markop tried to line up a shot and there was nowhere to stand. He stepped on a twig; dry trees and cobwebs caught in his hand. Then, mid-declaration, he stepped on **spider eggs**.
sections.waluigi_note: Three spiders closing in on the centaur with egg sacs underfoot. Stopping his own bleeding first with bandages before raising the heavy pike.

sections.name: V. Archie's Last High-Level Spell, Spent on a Bush
sections.overview:
Archie got out his spellbook. He erased some crossed-out words. He found his **last high-level spell**, one left, and circled it.

Then he said **FIREBALL**, loudly, and aimed at a bush.

The grove caught. Again. The same grove that burned in the Scorncrow skirmish is now burning a second time, lit deliberately by the party's own wizard, with the party still inside it.

Waluigi is not going to call that a mistake, because Markop had just asked for exactly this and the spiders were closing. Waluigi is going to note that the target was a bush, that the spell was the last one of its grade Archie had, and that everyone who was surrounded was still surrounded afterwards — now with a fire.
sections.waluigi_note: Circling the last spell slot with an ink pencil, roaring FIREBALL, and vaporizing an empty blackberry bramble. Magic spent on panic rather than line defense.

sections.name: VI. The Toads, Singing, Being Followed
sections.overview:
Elsewhere, entirely unaware:

*Well, glad we escaped, [Mossy](#/article/mossy). We almost died.* Then: *oh hey, [Wario](#/article/wario), we are staying away from danger.* Then, immediately: *that's great, let's get Wario on an adventure and explore to get out of here.*

And they began to sing. **We are the Toads, who broke our chains.**

Spiders followed the singing. The Toads did not notice. They walked faster. They sang faster. They ran through the grove singing faster.

Waluigi has filed this party singing during stealth before — it is in the Tymnas record — and files it again without further comment.
sections.waluigi_note: Singing hiking tunes while ettercaps stalk the tree canopy thirty feet overhead. Oblivious confidence in a hostile wetland.

sections.name: VII. The Extraction, and What It Cost the Guards
sections.overview:
The guards executed their plan. One sprinted, bolted, and **tripped**. Salam went down on the ground. A spider had him and dragged him further. Another guard, already injured, got him by a leg. They ended up **fireman-carrying** Salam out through the brood.

Markop, watching them go: *hey, where are you going?* To Legionhold hospital, the best in the area. Markop said he could heal him. The guard's answer — **he is scared, we can fix that right away** — is the most Legion sentence in the filing.
sections.waluigi_note: A sentry attempting a fireman carry over uneven roots, tripping, and losing his grip on the patient while spiders close the distance.

sections.name: VIII. Shatter, a Javelin, and a Barrier
sections.overview:
Archie saw Markop was desperate and used his own desperate move: he **shattered the space** around the spiders, and as it cleared, all of them were still standing.

Dan said he would make this quick, reached for his javelin, stopped, and **pointed one finger at Markop first** — sending a magical barrier across the grove to him — and only then threw.

The spider took the javelin and fell. Markop felt the heat of Archie's fireball going past.

*Either we go into the bark or the rope,* Dan said. Markop began the trek through the gauntlet, spiders on him the whole way, until he was out.

And then he got behind [Wario's motorbike](#/article/wario). He started it. He has **no idea what he is doing**.

Eager, meanwhile, killed an ettercap with a short sword, which the record notes because it is the only thing that went to plan.
sections.waluigi_note: Archie shattering the air around the perimeter; Dan stepping into the breach with an iron javelin to pin an ettercap to a cedar trunk.

sections.name: IX. The Wrights, the Torch, and the Door
sections.overview:
Remi ran into a room. Dark. *You have a torch?* — *Yeah, here,* said Wario. The light went up and showed them where they were: a room full of **wrights**.

One touched Remi. She screamed.

*Mossy, open the door.* The steel defender put its head into the wood and broke it open — and outside the door were spiders. Remi surrounded inside, spiders outside. *Should we fight everything, or the people in the room?*

She took the heavy battle axe in both hands and swung, and hit. The wright she hit **started glowing**. She swung again. Then she was hit, and it was **no longer glowing**, and Remi was freaking out.
sections.waluigi_note: Wario providing torchlight only to reveal a cellar packed with animated wrights. Illumination is rarely an improvement in this grove.

sections.name: X. Anamatar's Price
sections.overview:
Wario punched. Nothing happened. And then somebody came in from another room: **[Pierce Anamatar](#/article/pierce_anamatar)**.

*What are you doing here, fighting my people?*

*It hurt real bad. People chase me.*

*Aww, it hurt real bad. Want a bandaid? A sippy cup, maybe? Aww. Coward.* And: *you can't even handle a handful of knights. Stand down, my men.*

Wario said he was trying to get away from danger. Anamatar said he had come into his den and attacked him. Wario said he came to get away from the spiders. Anamatar asked whether he was afraid of a few creepy-crawlies.

Remi said the spiders were terrifying.

*Well.*

*Haven't you seen what they look like?*

And the mockery stopped, and the terms came out. This is a Guild-controlled area. He does not like the Guild. He will send them back where they came from **in exchange for something of theirs**.

He asked for the **siglet** — Tymnas's ring, the objective this party has been chasing for filings. An **expired coupon** was offered and declined. Then he walked over to Remi and asked for her card.

*I've got a single, very durable school ID card.*

***I'll take it.***

Remi handed over her student ID.
sections.waluigi_note: Pierce Anamatar blocking the doorway, demanding trade terms and safe conduct fees while monsters claw at the doorframe outside.

sections.name: XI. Where the Party Was When the Line Broke
sections.overview:
The grove did not present one fight with one front. It presented several emergencies occupying the same square of burning ground. The Scorncrow was already dead, but death had not made the position safe. The web ceiling held heat. The undergrowth caught again. The spiders moved through the smoke as if the fire had improved their options rather than reduced them. Every person making a decision was doing it from a different pocket of the same disaster.

Salam was down. Markop was still fighting with the consequences of the earlier engagement written across his body. Eager was unconscious enough to be carried and awake enough, at intervals, to object to the way he was being carried. Archie was spending the last useful spell in his book. Dan was trying to keep track of allies who kept vanishing behind bark, smoke, and web. Remi had been separated from the others and was doing inventory on herself because nobody else was in a position to do it for her.

That separation matters. The scene is often retold as though the Legion arrived, selected Eager, and removed him from an orderly party. It did not happen that way. The party was already failing to remain a single unit. The guards saw a casualty, a fire, a hostile grove, and a group that was arguing while the ground continued to worsen. Markop saw a squad member being taken. Both readings are true. The disagreement is not over what the grove looked like; it is over which truth grants authority.

The guard claimed the authority of the Legion code. Markop claimed the authority of membership. Eager, the person at the centre of it, claimed the authority to ask to be put down. Those authorities did not stack. They collided. No one produced a written order. No one paused long enough to establish consent, custody, or a route that everyone accepted. The decision happened because the next spider was already moving.
sections.waluigi_note: A tactical map of four separate factions stranded across two hundred yards of peat smoke with no working communications link.

sections.name: XII. The First Retreat Was Not an Airlift
sections.overview:
The word *airlift* entered the grove as reassurance. It promised distance without requiring the party to solve the ground in front of them. The guards said there was a helicopter and that they would put on a show. Archie would be taken to Legionhold. Salam would be transported. The sentence gave the retreat a future tense in which the party could imagine itself no longer standing in the fire.

Dan asked what a helicopter was. That question is not a joke inside the scene. It is a map of the gap between the people making the promise and the person expected to trust it. Dan came from a plane with no sky. The guard used a machine as if its existence were common knowledge. They were not arguing from the same world even before the question of Archie’s arrest entered the conversation.

The record contains no aircraft, landing, rotor wash, departure from the ground, or later arrival. What it contains is more difficult and more revealing: a sprint, a trip, Salam dragged by a spider, an already injured guard catching him by the leg, and Salam carried on foot. The promise was not merely delayed. Its physical substitute was a pair of people using their own bodies as transport.

That does not prove the helicopter never existed. It proves that the party did not receive the promised evacuation in this scene. The distinction belongs in the file because the Legion’s later credibility depends on it. A promise can fail because the asset was unavailable, because the speaker lied, because the route changed, or because nobody sent the request. The grove gives us the outcome and not the explanation.
sections.waluigi_note: The promised air extraction dissolved into an undignified scramble through brambles and muddy ditch-lines.

sections.name: XIII. The Cost of Getting Salam Out
sections.overview:
The extraction becomes less clean every time the record returns to it. The guards did not simply lift both bodies and walk away. One ran and tripped. Salam went down. A spider got him and pulled him farther into the brood. Another injured guard reached him by the leg. The rescue then became a contest between the spider’s grip, the guard’s grip, and the time remaining before the surrounding web caught fire or the next creature arrived.

That is the moment the party’s argument about competence acquires evidence. Markop said the party could heal its own. The Legion guard said the party had already demonstrated the opposite. While the dispute was active, Eager swung at a spider and struck the guard carrying Salam. The blow was not proof that Eager was careless; he was concussed, frightened, and being carried through a webbed battlefield. It was proof that the situation did not allow the guard to treat the party as a stable medical unit.

The guard’s line — *he is scared, we can fix that right away* — is cold because it turns fear into a condition the Legion can process. It is also the clearest statement of the institution’s confidence in itself. The party offers familiarity and loyalty. The Legion offers custody, equipment, and a place called a hospital. Neither side proves that its offer is safer. Salam leaves with the side that has enough people to carry them.
sections.waluigi_note: Two guards wounded and one stretcher abandoned in the thorns. The true balance sheet of a botched casualty evacuation.

sections.name: XIV. Remi’s Exit Is a Different Kind of Rescue
sections.overview:
Remi’s sequence should not be folded into the Legion extraction. She did not get carried out, and she did not leave because the grove became safe. She made herself mobile in stages. First she checked the blood and asked where it had come from. Then she removed the dress ruined by hooks. Then she took the chain shirt from a body. She looked at a shield and left it, a decision about weight and usefulness made while the rest of the grove was collapsing around her.

She healed herself once and found the result insufficient. She healed herself again and still did not call herself well. The line — *still not enough* — is not a victory speech. It is an inventory note from someone who knows the difference between being alive and being ready. She took the battle axe, accepted that the weapon changed what she could do, and walked out.

That is why the new armor matters to the visual record. Remi is not represented by one unchanging portrait after this scene. Her clothing, load, and weapon are evidence of a decision. She is a mid-teen adventurer, smaller than the adults around her but not a tiny child, and the chain shirt does not turn her into a soldier. It makes her a teenager who has scavenged enough protection to keep moving. The archive should show the change without pretending it is a new person.
sections.waluigi_note: Remi negotiating her own transit with Anamatar rather than waiting for an army that isn't coming. Pragmatic survival over military allegiance.

sections.name: XV. The Grove’s Last Sequence
sections.overview:
Markop’s escape begins only after the argument has moved past him. He is surrounded by three spiders, with no clean place to stand and spider eggs underfoot. He stops his bleeding, calls for a major spell, and then watches Archie erase words, find the final high-level spell, circle it, announce FIREBALL, and aim at a bush. The fire does not solve the encirclement. It changes the conditions of the encirclement.

Archie later shatters the space around the spiders. When the space clears, they are still standing. Dan does not answer the crisis by throwing first. He points at Markop, sends the barrier to him, and only then throws the javelin. The order matters. Protection comes before attack. The javelin drops one spider. Markop takes the route through bark and rope with spiders on him, then reaches Wario’s motorbike and starts it without knowing how to ride it.

The scene is full of people doing the next available thing rather than the ideal thing. Eager kills an ettercap with a short sword. The Toads run while singing and attract spiders by doing so. Remi enters a dark room, receives a torch, finds wrights, opens a door onto more spiders, and panics when the axe’s glow disappears. The grove does not sort these actions into competent and incompetent categories for us. It records sequence, cost, and who is still standing.
sections.waluigi_note: The fire joining across the canopy, turning the Skittering Grove into an enclosed furnace while survivors crawl through the low brush.

sections.name: XVI. The Price That Survives the Fire
sections.overview:
Anamatar’s den is the last threshold, but it is not a safe room. Wario enters while fleeing the spiders. Anamatar asks why strangers are fighting his people. The exchange begins as mockery — the bandaid, the sippy cup, the accusation that Wario cannot handle a handful of knights — and turns into terms when Wario admits that the spiders are terrifying.

The terms are specific. This is Guild-controlled ground. Anamatar does not like the Guild. He will send them back where they came from in exchange for something that belongs to them. The siglet is requested first. The expired coupon is offered and rejected. Then Remi’s student ID becomes the price. She hands over the card that still proves she attended Gehenna Academy, despite leaving without a formal withdrawal.

The exchange is not a triumphant escape. Three people get passage and Remi loses the last institutional paper attached to her name. The card is small, laminated, and described as durable. Its value in the scene is not durability. It is ownership. Anamatar takes an object that says who Remi was while she is trying to become someone who can survive the grove.

By the time the last people leave, the party has not achieved one shared retreat. The Legion has taken Salam on foot. Remi has escaped under her own power. Markop has crossed the gauntlet behind a barrier and a javelin. Wario’s group has purchased passage. The Toads remain in the dirt watching the others go. The word *airlift* describes what was promised, not what happened. What happened was a set of separate exits, each paid for differently.
sections.waluigi_note: Promissory notes, blood-stained bandages, and broken weapon hafts left behind in the mud for future archivists to catalogue.

sections.name: XVII. Standing
sections.overview:
The spiders closed. The guards ran, one supporting the fireman carry. Markop watched them come. Feyward Dan and Eager were surrounded.

And the three Toads, left in the dirt, watched every friendly character in the grove walk away from them.

WAH.
sections.waluigi_note: Spiders circling the perimeter, guards dragging stretchers, and three Toads wondering why the promised helicopter never arrived. WAH.

description:
Waluigi is going to file this one in the order it was argued, because the sentence that decides it was last spoken by the other side.

**Last filing, the Legion code took Salam away. Tonight the same words gave him back, and the only thing that changed was who was holding them.**
outcome: The Legion code has now been used in both directions. Markop rode the motorbike badly enough to find the guards who had not gotten Salam out of the grove, argued the awake man free with the Legion's own words, and assembled a sentry arrangement: Salam posted on the bike with a Legion guard, the retreat back through the tree of the grove, and a scream for a signal. A guard tried to move Salam off the bike — stand still, you worm — and was refused. An Iron Legion man ran past Markop in panic, cause unrecorded. The guards closed the night by healing Eager with a syringe. The party is still split, still in the grove, still upright — sixteen, eight, sixteen, eleven — and the scream has not been spent.

reputationNotes._record: The code was honoured in both directions in one night: the awake man was given back and the bitten one was patched. What the Legion's own running man thinks of the code is not on the record.

aftermath:
**The code has now been used both ways.** Last filing it took Salam; tonight Markop pointed it back, and the Legion let him go, left a guard waiting at the bike, and healed Eager with a syringe.

**Salam is awake and posted.** One spider shot, one missed, one refusal — 'stand still, you worm' answered with 'No!'

**Archie has been bitten by the giant green spider**, through Dan's temporary shield, with mana for one spell left in the book.

**Eager is bitten and slashed**, and being held still by the guards who say they will heal him.

**The three Toads are running up, deeper into the grove**, and may fully disengage if it turns south.

**Something made an Iron Legion man run past Markop in panic.** The record does not say what. The Toads are running toward it.

**Unresolved:** what the running man saw; where the tree of the grove lets out, and whether the way up is still open; whether the Toads disengage; and whether anyone will have to scream.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The code is symmetrical now, and the archive files symmetry.** One filing ago 'no man left behind' was a hand on a shoulder taking Salam to Legionhold. Tonight the same words, spoken by Markop, opened the same hand. Waluigi has no side to take anymore: the rule did exactly what it was asked to do, twice, by two different people, in opposite directions. That is what a code is. It is also why Waluigi does not write them.

**2. The plan is made of almosts, and it is still the best plan this party has produced in two filings.** A sentry who needs rest, a guard who an hour ago was the enemy, a retreat route through the throat of a tree nobody has surveyed, and a signal that is an unfinished sentence. Every component is inadequate. The assembly is sound. Waluigi has filed professional retreats that were worse.

**3. The syringe closed a loop the guards opened themselves.** 'He is scared, we can fix that right away' was filed one night ago as the most Legion sentence in the record. Tonight the fix arrived, and it was a needle, for the other side's scout, while their own man ran past in panic. The Legion does not love anyone. It processes. But the wound it processed was Eager's, and Eager is alive.

**4. The running man is the filing Waluigi cannot write yet.** Something in the deeper grove broke a professional soldier into a sprint, and the record gives it no name, no shape, and no direction except *up* — the same direction three Toads are travelling voluntarily. The archive will not guess. The archive will say plainly that it is watching that direction.

**Recommendation:** get to the tree before somebody has to scream.

WAH.

sections.name: I. The Worst First Ride in the Archive
sections.overview:
The filing opens where [the last one](#/article/the_airlift_that_never_came) ended: [Markop](#/article/markop) on [Wario](#/article/wario)'s motorbike, engine running, no idea what any of the controls do. What follows is the archive's first recorded centaur riding lesson, and it goes the way everything in the [Skittering Grove](#/article/skittering_grove) goes. He drove it poorly and rammed it into the trees; he bumped — the record's word, and Waluigi is keeping it — into [Salam](#/article/salam).

Consider what had to be true for that last part to happen. The Legion guards left this grove on foot, at a sprint, fireman-carrying an unconscious Toad through a burning wood. A man on a shoulder is not fast. A grove on fire rearranges its own paths. Somewhere between the exit they had promised themselves and the exit that exists, they were still there when a motorbike came off its line and found them — and the casualty they were carrying became the thing the motorbike hit.
sections.waluigi_note: A centaur on a goblin-built motorbike with no clutch experience is an aviation disaster waiting to ignite. Waluigi records that the throttle survived the oak tree.

sections.name: II. Let Him Go — He Is Awake
sections.overview:
The words came first: *let him go, he is awake.* Then [Salam](#/article/salam) made them true and woke up — his first recorded moment since the airlift carried him out of the frame. Two filings down. Face scarred from the clawing. On the ground between a guard's shoulder and a burning wood.

[Markop](#/article/markop) asked the question the whole arrangement now turned on: *can we go?*

The guard's answer began — *if you leave* — and the record cuts it there. Waluigi has spent longer than is professional on the rest of that sentence. If you leave, you are on your own. If you leave, we are not coming back. If you leave, the code stops applying. It does not matter, because Markop did not wait for it:

**"You said leave no one behind, right?"**

One filing ago that sentence was a hand on Salam's shoulder, walking him toward Legionhold over everyone's objection including Salam's. Tonight it was four words long and pointed back at the men who own them, and it worked. The guard let him go. An awake man is not a casualty, and a code that will not abandon a body has no clause for a person standing up and walking somewhere else.
sections.waluigi_note: Quoting an army's official field manual back to a sentry holding a weapon is dangerous literature. Markop made the code work by standing between the guard and the trees.

sections.name: III. Salam, You Rest
sections.overview:
What happened next was an order, and the order is the hinge of the filing. *Salam, you rest,* [Markop](#/article/markop) said. *Oh — okay. I got it,* said [Salam](#/article/salam), and took it.

Waluigi notes the transaction, because the archive has filed this party arguing about everything for two nights — about fire, about routes, about custody, about the definition of a helicopter — and the first command given and accepted all session was *rest*.

Then the plan, assembled out loud at the edge of the fire:

- [Salam](#/article/salam) waits at the motorbike, and a Legion guard waits with him. *You could just wait here, Salam. And you, guard.*
- [Markop](#/article/markop) goes to get his friends.
- If things get rough, the party is going back through the tree — the tree of the grove, the same throat the party roped down through when the grove first took them in.
- And Salam's options if it turns, named honestly, to his face: he might end up with these guards — *or on your own, but it won't be safe in this place.* *I hear you. Well, alright.*

And then the sentence this filing will be quoted by forever, delivered with its pause intact:

**"Don't leave. You just stay put. If we have to leave, I'll… scream for you."**

Waluigi has filed battle plans written by generals and evacuation protocols written by institutions, and he has never filed a signal that was an unfinished sentence. It is perfect: a scream carries through fire and web where orders do not, and nobody who hears one mistakes it for anything else.
sections.waluigi_note: An order to rest is the rarest command in this archive, and Salam took it without an argument because his ribs were whistling like an open flute.

sections.name: IV. The Toads Go Up
sections.overview:
The three [Toads](#/article/toads) made their own arithmetic on the far side of the grove. They would run upwards, deeper in. If it turned south, they may have to fully disengage.

*What if there is a guy up there?*

*I'll hope they're friendly… if not… I'll find a way out.*

The archive files both sentences without comment, in the same paragraph, next to each other, because that is the entire strategic doctrine of this party in two lines: hope first, exit second, no plan third.
sections.waluigi_note: The Toads made their own arithmetic in the dark. In this archive, scouts who plan their disengagement before the shouting begins are usually the ones who survive to be audited.

sections.name: V. A Legion Man Runs
sections.overview:
And then the filing's cold beat, the one Waluigi cannot explain and will not invent:

**An [Iron Legion](#/article/iron_legion) man ran past [Markop](#/article/markop) in panic.**

Not walked. Not withdrew. Ran, in the open, past an armed stranger, in the direction of out. The record does not say what he saw. The last time this archive watched the Legion in this grove, they were promising helicopters and grading everyone else's competence. Something in the deeper grove — the same deeper grove the three Toads have just decided to run toward — moved a professional soldier like that.

The archive does not know what it was, and notes only that it did not chase the man. Whatever it is, it let him go.
sections.waluigi_note: A trained legionary does not run from bad weather. Whatever was coming through the branches behind him had stripped six months of drill right out of his boots.

sections.name: VI. One Spell
sections.overview:
[Archie](#/article/archie_miser) ran toward the Toads on the other side of the grove. [Markop](#/article/markop) watched him go and shouted after him, and the distance between the two of them — two men calling across a burning wood — is this filing's geography.

*Great,* Archie called back. *I only have enough mana to use a single spell.*

One filing ago Archie erased the crossed-out lines in his spellbook and spent the last high-level spell in it on a bush. The well has a floor, and the floor is one spell of any size. And into the smoke, from someone — the record does not say who, and every one of them had earned the right to ask it — came the night's only honest question:

*How could this have happened?*

The arithmetic that answers it was called across the grove like a ledger being read out: [Markop](#/article/markop), sixteen. [Archie](#/article/archie_miser), eight. [Eager](#/article/eager), sixteen. [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad), eleven — nobody dead, nobody fit. Four numbers, none of them far enough from zero to matter, held by a party that is about to split — *I hate having to split up,* Markop said — inside a grove that just frightened the Iron Legion.

The split itself was argued properly. [Archie](#/article/archie_miser) was fine with leaving [Wario](#/article/wario) behind — Wario having already bought his way out through [Anamatar](#/article/pierce_anamatar)'s den at the price of [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory)'s student ID, a transaction Waluigi still cannot believe he gets to keep filing — but Salam, at least, should follow Markop. *If I go get Salam it will be too slow,* Markop answered. *Spiders will surround us.* And across the grove, Archie, in absolute earnest, shouted the question this archive has been waiting the whole campaign to hear:

**"Can Salam hold onto you?"**

A cavalry question, about a centaur, shouted across a burning wood — and the archive files it with joy.
sections.waluigi_note: Holding one spell in reserve while surrounded by things with mandibles is a severe test of character. Archie held the book shut until the grove demanded the fire.

sections.name: VII. Blades for a Doorway
sections.overview:
[Eager](#/article/eager) attacked with his blades — holding the spiders off, clearing a way for [Archie](#/article/archie_miser): a doorway made of one Toad swinging. [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) swung too, then looked around, put his head down, and put a shield around Archie, and told him to run.

The order of operations is the man. One filing ago Dan pointed one finger at Markop and sent the barrier across the grove before the javelin left his hand. Tonight he put his whole head down and put a shield around the wizard before he thought about himself at all. The archive has filed paladins who talk about protection. It keeps filing one who does it.

And from the motorbike — from the sentry post, from the rest Markop ordered — [Salam](#/article/salam) shot a spider. The man who left this grove unconscious on a Legion shoulder spent his first waking hour in two filings putting an arrow into the fight for his friends.
sections.waluigi_note: Eager made a doorway out of swinging steel. One Toad carving twenty seconds of free air for a wizard who was still trying to remember where he parked his boots.

sections.name: VIII. The Green One
sections.overview:
The way did not hold: [Archie](#/article/archie_miser), [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) and [Eager](#/article/eager) were surrounded.

[Eager](#/article/eager) got bitten and slashed; [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) dodged the attacks — all of them, and the filing notes a Toad paladin in a closing ring, unhittable, and unable to be everywhere at once. [Archie](#/article/archie_miser) was attacked by the giant green spider — the same green one that closed on Markop at the end of the last filing, patient as an institution — and it bit him, and Dan's temporary shield broke.

That spider has now attended two filings, menaced a centaur, and bitten a wizard through a shield made by a paladin who does not miss. It is the best fighter in the grove and it is owed a file of its own.
sections.waluigi_note: The giant green spider did not negotiate. It closed the perimeter like an experienced bailiff with eight legs and an overactive venom gland.

sections.name: IX. Stand Still, You Worm
sections.overview:
At the motorbike, a guard decided the sentry arrangement had run its course and tried to grab [Salam](#/article/salam) off the bike.

*Stand still, you worm.*

**"No!"**

Two filings ago Salam was carried out of this grove unconscious, on a shoulder, over an objection he was not awake to make. Tonight, awake, under orders, one arrow into the fight, he refused the hands. And the next thing the record shows him doing is drawing the bow again.

Spiders approached [Markop](#/article/markop), and a spear was rammed into the ettercap. The record does not say whose spear, in a grove containing Legion guards who carry them and a party whose javelin left in the last filing. Waluigi files his suspicion nowhere.
sections.waluigi_note: Calling a wounded Toad a worm while trying to repossess him for a military hospital tab is standard Legion bedside manner. Salam's refusal was his best line all night.

sections.name: X. The Syringe
sections.overview:
And then the Legion closed the night by closing its own loop.

The guards said they would heal [Eager](#/article/eager). *Stand still.* One got out a syringe.

One filing ago, over Markop's offer to heal his own man, a guard said: *he is scared, we can fix that right away.* Waluigi filed it then as the most Legion sentence in the record. He files the syringe now as that sentence made physical: an institution that processes fear, and wounds, and objections, through procedure. The same organisation that carried a man out on the code one filing ago put a man back together on the same night, with the same certainty, while its own soldier was running past in the other direction.

The code, paid in both directions within the hour. Waluigi did not expect to file that.
sections.waluigi_note: The Legion's idea of roadside first aid is an iron needle the size of a knitting needle shoved through combat fatigues without an antiseptic wipe.

sections.name: XI. Standing
sections.overview:
The position as this filing closes:

[Archie](#/article/archie_miser), [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) and [Eager](#/article/eager) surrounded — Archie bitten through a broken shield with one spell of mana left in the book; Eager bitten and slashed and being held still for a syringe; Dan untouched and unable to fix either of those things. [Markop](#/article/markop) at the motorbike with spiders approaching. [Salam](#/article/salam) on the motorbike, awake, under orders, refusing hands, one arrow spent and one missed. A Legion guard beside him who has been told to wait. The three [Toads](#/article/toads) somewhere above, running deeper into the thing that made a soldier run.

And strung between the bike and the surrounded, unspent, the arrangement: *if we have to leave, I'll… scream for you.*

Nobody has screamed yet. Waluigi has attended a great many battles, and he reports that the sound everybody is listening for is the one nobody wants to make.

WAH.
sections.waluigi_note: The code came back the other way, the scream was still trapped in Archie's throat, and the grove was about to demand the rest of the bill. WAH.

name: The Way I Started It
title: The Way I Started It: Fireball, Whispered — the Fall of Feyward Dan, Two Hit Points, and the Fist That Closed the Grove
date: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — straight on from the sentry arrangement; the scream gets made, and it is not the signal
era: Raventree Crisis — Shadeward Operations / The Skittering Grove / Post-Scorncrow Collapse
location: The Skittering Grove — the grove floor between the fires, the deeper trees Archie ran into, and the stump the plan was built around
type: Grove Battle / Last Spell / Fighting Withdrawal Concluded
status: Concluded — the giant green spider and the ettercaps are dead, Feyward Dan fell and was healed back up, Eager is on two hit points, Archie is out of spells, and the party is going back to the stump to rest instead of after Remi
summary: Straight on from the sentry arrangement. Archie runs deeper into the forest and Eager follows and kills the giant green spider — the grove's best fighter, dead to a Toad scout with blades. Dan, one-armed, drops the longsword for the shield and sets himself to defend the party; Markop watches everyone run away from the actual stump the plan was built around, and stays at it, revving Wario's motorbike. Dan is webbed and falls, and the scream the last filing was listening for gets made — by Archie, for Dan, and not as the signal. Eager wrestles the ettercap and throws Dan to Archie; the catch is missed. Archie puts the body down, faces the ettercaps — 'I'll end this journey the way I started it, with my signature spell' — and whispers Fireball with a tear in his eye. Two ettercaps left, Archie out of spells; Eager's final stand takes one, and he walks backwards into Markop: 'Hello.' Salam puts the bow down and heals Dan; Markop's healing keeps Eager alive at two hit points; Eager takes the electric sphere; Markop shoves Eager aside and ends the last ettercap with his fist. aftermath:
**The grove is fought through.** The giant green spider, two filings a menace and owed a file, is dead to Eager's blades; the ettercaps are dead to a whispered Fireball, a final stand and a fist. The archive marks the Skittering Grove fight concluded.

**Feyward Dan fell and is up.** Webbed, dropped at zero, dropped again on the catch, healed by Salam. The Permanent Injury Table gave him 59 — Sprained Thumb, one week — the one row that costs a one-armed paladin nothing he had.

**Eager has two hit points** and the electric sphere. The record says the sphere was powered during the giant battle by Archie's electric magic; the archive has no earlier sighting of it and files the claim as stated.

**Archie is out of spells.** 'Without my spells I am useless.' The first real Fireball on his record was his last one.

**The party is going back to the stump to rest**, over Markop's objection — 'what about Remi, we can't rest now' — which the Toads answered with 'Eager can handle his own' and 'Salam is weak.'

**The Iron Legion appears nowhere in this filing.** The guard posted at the bike, the medic, the man who ran — none of them is on the record while the ettercaps closed.

**Unresolved:** Remi, and whether Markop accepts the vote; what the Legion did while the grove was fought; whether the three Toads who ran upward are the Toads who voted; what the electric sphere is and what it will do in Eager's hands; what made the Legion man run — the ettercaps are a candidate, not an answer.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The plan held at exactly one point, and nobody went to it.** The stump was agreed by everyone and used by one. Markop stood where the arrangement put him and watched the arrangement leave. The eight lines he and Eager exchanged at the end — *I thought you left me for dead* / *I was talking to you* — are the whole failure in dialogue: a signal that meant something else, a rally point that nobody rallied to, and two people who were each right. Waluigi files the plan as sound and the party as somewhere else.

**2. The table's own post-mortem is the correct one, and the archive declines to improve on it.** Archie used every crowd-control spell he had and everyone left the space they bought. The archive has written that sentence in three different ways across three grove filings — the airlift, the scream pact, the stump — and would like it on the record that the players wrote it themselves tonight, which is the first time.

**3. The whispered Fireball is filed as a first, not a last.** Archie has threatened this spell for the length of the archive; the first one that was real was cast with nothing behind it, over a friend he had just put down, and it was whispered. Waluigi does not file sentiment. He files volume, and notes that a man who says *this may be the end of us* and then ends it for three ettercaps instead has described the fight accurately in every respect but the subject.

**4. Row 59.** The one-armed paladin drew the one injury in a hundred that forbids things he cannot do. The archive, which authored the table and locked it, did not plan this and would not have dared.
