sections.name: I. Deeper in
sections.overview:
[Archie](#/article/archie_miser) ran. Not to the bike and not to the tree: deeper, into the forest, after the three [Toads](#/article/liberated_toads) who had gone up a filing ago toward whatever made a Legion man run. Markop, at the motorbike, watched [Eager](#/article/eager) swing a sword and follow him.

Then Eager killed the big spider.

The archive would like a moment. The giant green spider closed on Markop in one filing, bit Archie through a paladin's shield in the next, and was described in this file — accurately — as the best fighter in the grove and owed a page of its own. It died to a [Toad](#/article/toads) scout with blades, somewhere past the fires, with no ceremony the record kept. Waluigi opens its file and closes it in the same sentence, which is more than it did for anybody.
sections.waluigi_note: The giant green spider closed on Markop in one filing, bit Archie through a paladin's shield in the next, and was described as the best fighter in the grove. It died to a Toad scout with short blades, past the ash, with no ceremony. Waluigi opens its file and closes it in the same sentence, which is more than it did for anybody.

sections.name: II. One arm, two tools
sections.overview: [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) has one arm. The archive has filed the arm before and files it again here because it decided the next thing he did. With the ring closing, he dropped the longsword and took up the shield — the one-handed shield, the only one a one-armed man can use — and set himself to defend the party. A man who can hold one thing chose the thing that protects other people. Waluigi records the arithmetic without comment, which for Waluigi is a comment.
sections.waluigi_note: A man who can hold only one thing chose the tool that protects other people instead of the steel that protects himself. Waluigi records the arithmetic without comment, which for Waluigi is a comment.

sections.name: III. The stump
sections.overview:
Here is the beat Markop will be telling for the rest of his life. He stood at the stump — the actual stump, the planned escape point, the thing agreed an hour ago by every person now running — and watched the whole party run away from it in every other direction. He stayed. He revved the motorbike.

[Salam](#/article/salam) fired from the bike. Markop revved again and left an ettercap in the dust, which the archive files as the machine's first useful act since it hit a tree.
sections.waluigi_note: Revving an idling motorbike in the dark to blow gravel into an ettercap's eyes is the machine's first useful act since it hit a pine tree two filings ago.

sections.name: IV. The scream
sections.overview:
Dan got webbed. Feyward Dan fell. Archie screamed.

One filing ago the arrangement ended with a line the archive underlined: *if we have to leave, I'll… scream for you.* The scream was the signal. It was the sound everybody was listening for and nobody wanted to make. Tonight it was made — and it was not the signal. It was a wizard watching a paladin go down, and nobody retreated on it, because the thing it was supposed to mean had already stopped being possible. Waluigi files the scream as the plan's last word: made on schedule, meaning something else.

Eager wrestled the ettercap off Dan and threw Dan to Archie. The body fell. A Toad threw a Toad to a wizard, and the catch was not made. The record does not say whether the throw was short or the hands were slow, and the archive does not care: it says Dan hit the ground a second time, which is one more time than a man with no hit points should.
sections.waluigi_note: The scream was agreed as the retreat signal that nobody wanted to make. Tonight it was torn out of a wizard watching a paladin drop, and nobody retreated because retreat had already stopped being possible. Made on schedule, meaning something else entirely.

sections.name: V. The way I started it
sections.overview:
Archie held the body. The record says he thought about running, and the archive believes it, because he said so himself and because the archive has his file. Then he put Dan down, and stood up, and faced the ettercaps.

*This may be the end of us, or me, as we know it. I may not have been good — but at least I'll end this journey the way I started it. With my signature spell.*

He whispered it. **Fireball.** A tear in his eye. It exploded.

The archive needs to be careful here, because it has filed a great many of Archie's fireballs. It has filed the one he charged in a corridor full of screaming pirates, the one he faked in this grove before delivering a firebolt instead, and the one Markop begged him for a filing ago — *use fireball, use your lightning, anything* — which did not come. It has filed the threat more times than it can count: *I can just fire a ball at you.* Tonight was the first time the archive saw the real one, and it was whispered, by a man with nothing in the book behind it, over a friend he had just set down. Waluigi files the volume.

Two ettercaps were still standing when the light went out of it. Archie was woozy and out of spells. The book is empty. Whatever the party does next, it does without him, and he knows it.
sections.waluigi_note: Archie has threatened fireball in hallways, faked it in the grove, and held it back when begged. This was the first time the real one arrived, whispered over a friend set down in the dirt with nothing left in the book behind it. Waluigi files the volume.

sections.name: VI. Two hit points
sections.overview:
Eager's final stand took one of the two. One left.

Then he raged, stepped back, stumbled, and walked backwards into Markop, who had not moved. The exchange is on the record and the archive gives it whole, because it is the plan and its failure in eight lines:

**"Hello."**

**"I thought you left me for dead for a moment."**

**"I said come towards me, to the tree. I don't know what you're talking about — I was talking to you."**

**"We were surrounded."**

**"Don't worry, I'm healthier than the other guys."**

**"Are you sure? You're bleeding."**

**"Yes I am. It's been a rough fight."**

**"I don— don't disagree."**

Markop stayed where the plan put him. Eager thought he had been abandoned. Both of them are right, and Waluigi has stopped expecting that to be unusual.

Salam grabbed his bow, put it down again, and went to Dan instead. He healed him up. The sentry left the post he had been given to put his hands on the fallen man, and the archive files it under the only order Salam has received all night — *rest* — being disobeyed for the second time, correctly.

Eager took an attack that should have finished him and did not, because Markop had put healing into him first. Two hit points. Critical. The archive carried the ledger across the grove in the last filing — Markop sixteen, Archie eight, Eager sixteen, Dan eleven — and files the new line without the rest: Eager, two.

Battered, worn, scattered. Somewhere in this Eager picked up the electric sphere — the record says it was powered during the giant battle by Archie's electric magic, and the archive has no earlier sighting of the thing and says so. It is on the technology ledger now, with Eager's name beside it and a question mark beside his.
sections.waluigi_note: Markop stayed where the plan put him; Eager thought he had been abandoned. Both men were right, and Waluigi has stopped expecting that to be unusual in this grove.

sections.name: VII. The fist
sections.overview:
The last ettercap was still alive. One hit point, by the table's own count: the same number Eager was two away from. Markop pushed Eager aside and smacked it down with his fist.

The grove took a scythe, a thunder-called warhammer, a javelin thrown across its full length, a whispered fireball, and most of a paladin. It ended on a punch, from the man who never left the stump. Waluigi files that with something he declines to name.
sections.waluigi_note: The grove took a scythe, a thunder-called warhammer, a javelin thrown across its full length, a whispered fireball, and most of a paladin. It ended on a bare knuckle punch from the man who never left the stump. Waluigi files that with something he declines to name.

sections.name: VIII. The stump, again
sections.overview:
They picked up their stuff. Then the argument, which was short:

*"What about Remi? We can't rest now."* — Markop.

*No.* The Toads were going back to the stump.

*"Without my spells I am useless."* — Archie.

*"If you want the party to come help, we will be useless."* The Toads, pressing the case against going anywhere. *"Eager can handle his own."* *"Salam is weak."*

Back to the stump. Markop's question is the only mention of [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) in the record tonight, and the archive files it as a lead, because the man who asked it was outvoted and is bleeding and the record does not show him agreeing.
sections.waluigi_note: Markop's question is the only mention of Remi in the record tonight. He was outvoted, exhausted, and bleeding, and the record does not show him agreeing.

sections.name: IX. The post-mortem, which the table held itself
sections.overview: Archie used all his crowd-control spells, and everyone left. That is the main problem with the battle, and it is not the archive's reading — it is the table's own, offered unprompted and filed verbatim. The spells bought a space; nobody stood in it. The stump was the plan; nobody went to it until they walked into it backwards. The record calls that a lesson. The archive calls it the same lesson as the last two filings with the furniture rearranged, and files it anyway.
sections.waluigi_note: The table calls this a tactical lesson. The archive calls it the exact same failure as the last two filings with the furniture rearranged, and files it anyway.

sections.name: X. The table
sections.overview:
The one who fell gets the table. The archive rolled the Permanent Injury Table for Feyward Dan, as the house rule requires, and the die gave **59 — Sprained Thumb**: *you cannot fight with two weapons, and attack rolls with a versatile weapon used two-handed are made at disadvantage. Rest — one week.*

Waluigi would like the record to appreciate this. Of a hundred rows — death at the bottom, a limb at five, scars, trauma, the slow rows that take a year to walk off — the die found the one injury that costs a one-armed paladin nothing he had. He has never fought with two weapons. He will never hold a versatile weapon in two hands. The thumb is real and it is splinted and he will carry it for a week, and the rule it carries is addressed to a man who does not exist. Waluigi files it as the grove's last joke, and the kindest thing it did all night.
sections.waluigi_note: Of a hundred rows on the steel ladder, the die found the one injury that costs a one-armed paladin nothing. The thumb is real and splinted, but the rule applies to a body he does not have. The kindest joke the grove produced all night.

sections.name: XI. Standing
sections.overview:
The position as this filing closes:

The giant green spider and the ettercaps are dead. Feyward Dan is up, webbed, one thumb in a splint, one week on the rule. Eager has two hit points and a sphere that hums. Archie has no spells and knows what that makes him. Salam is weak and said so by proxy. Markop is bleeding, is healthier than the other guys, and is the only one who was where the plan said. The [Iron Legion](#/article/iron_legion) — the guard at the bike, the medic with the syringe, the man who ran — appears nowhere in this filing; where it was while the ettercaps closed is not something the archive can say. [Wario](#/article/wario), Remi and [Mossy](#/article/mossy) are still on the far side of a passage somebody else paid for.

Five people are going back to the stump to rest, which is where they were supposed to be an hour ago, before any of this.

WAH.

name: The Box at the Cottage Door
title: The Box at the Cottage Door: Eight Hours Counted, a Girl in a Parcel, the Midnight Fountain Lit, and a Ship That Was Not Theirs Anymore

summary: The party rests eight hours in Tymnas's cottage and loots the grove's dead. The stump burns down, closing the exit. Green T knocks with a delivery — a box with Remi asleep inside. Archie wants to kill the oracle; the table settles on the ritual, Green T lights the Midnight Fountain, and the party steps out at the ruined manor. At the Legionlance a guard named Mr. Shock swings a baton at Remi, a doctor produces a bone saw, and Markop pulls her out by the hand. In the town below, a guard orders them to smile for Kyle Coinsoul's execution; Remi sells half her kit, Archie buys packs, Markop buys binoculars and sees Toads in rags storming the ship, and Dan is given a name for a prosthetist.
description:
*Waluigi has filed the Scorncrow, the Skittering Grove and the long fall of the Shadow Estate as a single wound. This is the filing where it closes: the exit burns, a girl is delivered in a parcel, a candle is lit, and everybody goes home to find that home has a new owner. WAH!*

The filing opens on a cottage and closes on a shop counter. In between, it is the shortest ritual in the archive — a beam, a step, a ruined manor — and the longest argument about a gold bar.

It has no combat in it. Markop swings once, at the gate; what the swing met is not on the table. It has no spells, no casualties and no villain. What it has is a party that has just survived the worst night of its campaign and is, for the first time in a month, at the mercy of nothing more than a shopkeeper's exchange rate and a guard's temper.
outcome: The party leaves the Shadowfell by the Midnight Fountain ritual and arrives at the ruined manor near Thornwood. The grove exit burned. Remi is recovered, alive, with no account of her disappearance. The Legionlance is Legion-held and, as the party watches, being stormed by Toads in rags. A Legion guard has announced the execution of Kyle Coinsoul under Commander G. The party has binoculars, ink, two packs, a crossbow case and a candle, thirty-one gold from the bar and the earring, and a rumour about a prosthetist.

aftermath:
**The exit is gone.** The stump burned. Whatever the party does next about the Shadowfell, it will not be through that tree.

**Remi is back and unexplained.** She was delivered by Green T and has a theory about sleepwalking. The archive has no account of where she went between the grove and the box.

**Three people stayed behind and nobody said so.** Bones, Hjumpik and Toad Lee were not mentioned at the fountain. They are, as of this filing, on the other side.

**The Legionlance is being stormed.** Through a pair of binoculars bought for the purpose. The result is not seen.

**Kyle Coinsoul is to be executed.** A town guard said so, and said Commander G will preside.

**Dan has a name.** Rudy Lee. One shopkeeper's rumour.

**The grove paid out.** A giant green spider's eye (Eager), a coil of ettercap silk (Markop), a vial of ettercap venom (Archie) and a giant spider's fang (Dan).
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The ritual took a paragraph.** The Midnight Fountain was the way out of the Shadowfell the whole time, and the party walked into the beam in less time than it took to argue about a bar of gold. The archive files the ritual as the cheapest part of the exit.

**2. Archie's oracle is a debt the archive cannot read.** He remembered a conversation, a condition and a jerk, and none of the three has a source. He chose the ritual over the oracle in the same breath. File it as unresolved, not as dropped.

**3. Remi's box is the unanswered question of the filing.** She went missing in a grove full of ettercaps and came back asleep. Green T delivered her and said a friend had sent her. Markop asked who; the answer was Archie stopping in the middle of a word. The archive lists Green T as the only person who could say.

**4. Mr. Shock told the party the truth.** The ship is not theirs anymore. The Toads, in rags, were already doing something about it. Waluigi would like his ship back and has told nobody that he is hoping for the rags.

**5. The party sold a bar for a third of its worth and was angry about it for one line.** The shop was the only place in the filing where anyone was cheated, and it was done politely, in the morning, with Eager asking someone to interject.

**Recommendation:** find out where Remi was. Then ask Green T who his friend was. Then count the people on the other side of the fountain.

sections.name: I. Eight Hours, Counted
sections.overview:
The stump was the plan, so they went back to it, and then — because the grove was still burning somewhere behind them and nobody could think of anything cleverer — they went to the only building in the Shadowfell with a warm hearth in it. [Tymnas's cottage](#/article/tymnas_cottage_and_hedge_maze) took them in through its low door and did not ask what the blood was.

They rested eight hours, and the table said plainly that those eight counted.

They looted all the bodies. Every one the grove had left was turned out — ettercaps, spiders, the lot — and what came off them went onto the sheets: an eye cut from the giant green spider for [Eager](#/article/eager), who had killed it; a coil of ettercap silk for [Markop](#/article/markop); a vial of ettercap venom for [Archie](#/article/archie_miser); and a spider's fang for [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad). Then Markop and the rest lay down, and the hearth was the only light.
sections.waluigi_note: A spider grove pays in spider. An eye, a coil of silk, a vial of venom and a fang, off a night that cost Dan a thumb, Archie every spell he had and Eager all but two hit points. Waluigi has seen worse exchange rates. He sees one eleven sections from now.

sections.name: II. The Exit Goes
sections.overview:
The fire finally reached the stub of the tree — the stump the plan had been built around, in the ruined manor grounds — and it burned it down.

The exit was gone.

The table said it in one flat sentence and did not dwell. A way out that [Archie](#/article/archie_miser) had made by burning something had been unmade by the same fire.
sections.waluigi_note: Archie sealed the way back with fire in the last filing and the fire finished the job in this one. The party did not choose to be shut in. It is simply true that, by the time anyone woke, the tree route was not a route.

sections.name: III. A Knock, a Delivery, a Window
sections.overview:
The knock came at the door. A voice outside said it was a delivery, and that it was for Markop.

Markop went to the window rather than the door and looked out. [Green T](#/article/green_t) was standing on the step with a box in his arms.

"Where were you, Green T?"

"I was getting backup. Then you guys left without me and I couldn't go through with my plan."

"What plan?"

"I'm sorry — *backup*?" Archie said, from somewhere behind Markop's flank.

"The plan was to escape and destroy the grove for good. I was gathering fey to help. The plan didn't work when no one showed up."

"You're friends with fey," Markop said.

"You mean fairies," said Archie.

"I'm not friends with fey. They're friends with money." Green T shifted the box on his forearm. "Either way, I've got a delivery from you."

"From who?"

"A friend. An associate of the Green Tea Syndicate."

"Who?" Markop said.

"I thought I destroyed them. They're all de—" Archie said, and stopped himself in the middle of the word.
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi has watched Green T be underestimated for a living. Here he is underestimated by a man who cannot finish the word *dead*. *Friends with money* is the cleanest self-description on file for the Syndicate, and he gave it standing in a doorway holding a parcel.

sections.name: IV. The Box
sections.overview:
"Who are these friends of yours, Green T?" Archie asked.

"Check the box," Green T said.

Archie opened the door and took it. It was kind of heavy. He decided the box seemed fine and carried it in. Markop, who had the better reach, undid the lid.

[Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) was asleep inside it.

She woke to a horse's face a foot over her own, with the other faces crowding in behind it, and the first thing she said was, "A— how did I get here?"

"Where did you go?" said somebody.

"Don't worry about it," said Remi.

"Where's Wario?" Archie asked. "Where's that Misley?"

"We were going back to the tree to help you," Markop said.

"I could use a nap," said Remi, and curled up in the box.

"You were just resting. Get up."

Markop picked her out of it by the scruff and stood her on the floor, which in his hands was a matter of one motion.

"Thanks for saving her," Archie told the window.
sections.waluigi_note: A fourteen-year-old girl went into a spider grove under her own power, vanished from every account for the length of a rest, and was delivered back to the stump's doorstep by a man who had been looking for backup. Waluigi has the box, the step and the lid. He does not have the middle.

sections.name: V. How Did I Even Get There
sections.overview:
"How did I even get there?" Remi said. "Oh — well. Doesn't matter. Maybe I sleepwalked."

"Are you sure?" Eager said. "There were ettercaps swimming around."

"I'm not sure. But I'm here now."

That was the end of it, for the table. It had the girl, in one piece, rested, with a theory about sleepwalking, and it had a man on the doorstep who had said he came with a delivery and had delivered it. Nobody asked Green T a second time.

Eager put the next question on the floor. "What's our plan going forward? Everyone's safe. We killed the Scorncrow."

"I don't know," said Markop.
sections.waluigi_note: The Scorncrow is dead and, by the party's own count, everyone is safe. Waluigi files both statements and notes that neither of them was true twenty minutes earlier and that the girl they were true about did not walk back in on her own feet.

sections.name: VI. The Oracle, or the Ritual
sections.overview:
Archie said what he wanted. "I want to kill the oracle. Based on a conversation I had. We kill it or we're stuck here forever."

"What are you saying?" Markop asked. "We can take the tree route we found, or we do the ritual with Green T."

"I don't remember the conversation," Archie said, "but I know that if I don't kill the oracle I may never leave here."

"Why?"

"I don't know. Because the person who ordered the condition is a jerk."

"Archie," Markop said. "You left this dimension about eight hours ago."

"Oh. I thought it was days ago."

He thought about it. The table watched him do it. Then Archie said they were doing the ritual and that was all, and Markop said that, in that case, he guessed they were doing the ritual.

Remi volunteered to lead it.

"Why?" said Markop.

"Because of adventure."

A beat, then Remi again: "Shouldn't Green T be up front?"
sections.waluigi_note: Archie remembers a conversation he cannot place, from a person he has not named, imposing a condition he cannot describe, about a creature nobody has seen, and he is certain enough of it to propose murder. The archive keeps the sentence. It has never been wrong to keep one of his.

sections.name: VII. The Midnight Fountain
sections.overview:
They set the ritual up. Green T walked the ring of the [Midnight Fountain](#/article/shadow_estate) lighting the candles around it, one by one. Then the beam came — straight down from the heavens, no flare, no warning — and they walked into it.

They came out at the ruined manor.

"We can leave," somebody said. "We can go home."

"Let's go to a town for now and get our bearings," Archie said.

"That sounds like a great idea," said Remi.

"Alright," said Markop.

"They're looking for me here," Archie said. "Let's go."

That was all the farewell the Shadowfell got. Bones, Hjumpik and Toad Lee had all been left behind in it, and not one person at the fountain said a word about it.
sections.waluigi_note: The Midnight Fountain has been the way out of the Shadowfell since the first filing, and the ritual itself takes a paragraph. Three people were left on the wrong side of the beam and nobody said anything. Waluigi is saying it for them. WAH.

sections.name: VIII. Whose Airship
sections.overview:
The first thing they saw of the world was the ship. The [Vigilance](#/article/vigilance) — [the Legionlance](#/article/vigilance), now — was moored where they had last seen it, and there was a guard on the gangway.

Remi ran straight at him. "HEY! WHAT'S YOUR NAME?"

"What's yours?" the guard asked.

"Remi."

"Remi. That sounds familiar. Are you on the wanted list?"

"What's your name, sir?"

"Mr. Shock."

"Shock who — *woah*."

She ducked the baton. [Mr. Shock](#/article/mr_shock) had swung it, and she had moved.

"Why did you do that? It wasn't very nice. How could you be not nice, Mr. Shock?"

"Well, I'm sorry. I'm just a bit twitchy."

"Twitchy?"

"Yes. If anyone passes this threshold, they'd end up in custody."

"Whose custody?"

"The Legion's. This is the Legionlance — our top-of-the-line airship."

"Wait. But this is *our* airship."

"Not anymore," the guard said.

Markop swung.
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi has said *Legionlance* is a terrible name for this ship in print. Here it is spoken by a man with a shock baton who is just a bit twitchy, and the name is no better. The record ends on Markop's swing. What the swing met is not on the table. WAH.

sections.name: IX. The Doctor with the Saw
sections.overview:
"Come over here, sir," said a voice from behind the gate guard. "This one's rowdy."

A medieval doctor came over. "Yes — what's the problem, sir? Do you need medicine?"

"He hurt my friend," Markop said.

"Come here, little one," said the doctor to Remi, and held up a bone saw.

A Toad on the gangway said, "You're going to the glue factory."

"We're going to go," Markop said.

Remi ran to the doctor.

Markop caught her by the hand and hauled her away. "Nooo," she said, all the way down the plank.

"You have such a way with words," said Green T. He was standing off to one side, outside the gate, watching them go past. He fell in behind them, slowly, at the pace of somebody with all the time in the world.
sections.waluigi_note: A girl who has just been dug out of a box, and who was not sure how she got in it, ran toward a man holding a saw because he said *little one*. Markop held her hand and did not let go. Waluigi gives the whole scene to Markop and the line to Green T.

sections.name: X. Smile
sections.overview:
They went into the town. A guard stopped them at the edge of it.

"What are you guys doing out so early?"

"Long story short," Archie said, "we found this town nearby and thought we could stay for a few."

"Oh, that's great. Just put on a smile while you're here. The top legionnaire, Kyle Coinsoul, is coming."

"So in other words he owns all the stores here," said Archie.

"No, no, no. Kyle Coinsoul is being *killed*. An execution, if you will. He stole. And the top legionnaire, Commander G, will be overseeing it."

Markop asked whether the guard happened to know where he might find a pair of binoculars, and where the shop was.

"Over there."

They all walked up.
sections.waluigi_note: The archive has [Kyle Coinsoul](#/article/kyle_coinsoul) as a Guild man with gambling debts and an override key. This guard has him as a top legionnaire who stole. [Commander G](#/article/commander_g) is *top legionnaire* here too. Waluigi will take the guard's word for the execution and nobody's for the ranks.

sections.name: XI. The Shop
sections.overview:
Markop bought his binoculars. [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) went through her inventory looking for things to sell and found, at the bottom, a container of brain juice.

"Brain juice? When did I have *brain juice*?"

She put her hand on a magnifying glass on the counter. It was a hundred gold. She had twenty-five.

So she sold things. Her ink — which, she told the room, could have written five hundred pages of whatever — went for two bronze. Her bullet casings, the ones that nearly killed the orange heir, went for sixty-five gold. A coupon from Angel 24 went for five. Her book on plant identification went for fifteen.

[Archie](#/article/archie_miser) asked the shopkeeper what the ink she had just sold would cost.

"Ten gold."

He bought it, with an entertainer's pack, a diplomat's pack, a crossbow case and a candle. Remi watched him pay for her ink. "Wow," she said.

Then Archie put a bar of gold on the counter. The shopkeeper offered fifteen. It was worth fifty.

"What?" said Eager. "Someone please interject. Someone, please."

Nobody did.

"I've got it," said [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad), and stepped up. "Hey. My turn. Sorry — we're going to sell this to you. How much will you give us?"

"Fifteen gold."

"How much if we give you this earring?"

"Sixteen."

They sold both: fifteen and sixteen, thirty-one gold. Remi kept hers in her pocket and left the magnifying glass where it was.
sections.waluigi_note: Her ink went for two bronze and came back at ten gold. The bar was worth fifty. Fifteen and sixteen is thirty-one, which is eighteen short of what the bar alone was worth.

sections.name: XII. Through the Glass
sections.overview:
While the others were still at the counter, Markop put the binoculars to his eyes and turned them on the ship.

He could see the deck. He could see two people lying on the deck, the two from earlier — and, over the rail and up the gangway, Toads. They were storming the ship. A flag went up. Somewhere, a trumpet sounded and a horn answered it, and the whole line of them went forward at once.

"CHARGE."

"Liberated Toads," Eager asked, "or loyalists?"

"They're wearing rags," Archie said. "They're our group."
sections.waluigi_note: The archive has three guards on the gate and a doctor with a saw, and then four lines of dialogue and a trumpet. [The Liberated Toads](#/article/liberated_toads) took the Legionlance, or were taking it, at the exact minute the party was selling a bar of gold for a third of its worth. Nobody saw the end. WAH.

sections.name: XIII. Doctor Rudy
sections.overview:
Before they went, Dan stopped at the counter.

"Do you know a guy who can make us prosthetic arms? I lost my arm. I was wondering if there's someone in this town."

"Hmm. There might be one person."

"What's the rumour?"

"They're very hands on with their prosthetics."

"What do you mean by that?"

"They like to do it while the person's awake."

"Is there a reason for that?"

"Not sure."

"We'll keep it in mind. Who's the person who can give us the arm?"

"Their name is Rudy Lee."

"Doctor Rudy," Dan said. "Got it."
sections.waluigi_note: [Rudy Lee](#/article/rudy_lee) is one rumour from one shopkeeper who was not sure why. A man with one arm heard *while the person's awake* and said *got it*. Waluigi would like to be present at the second question and does not expect to be.

sections.name: XIV. Standing
sections.overview:
The position as this filing closes:

The party is out of the Shadowfell. The [Scorncrow](#/article/scorncrow) is dead, the tree is a stump that has burned, the grove is behind them and the exit they came through is gone. Remi is alive, rested and unexplained. Green T followed them out at a walking pace. Bones, Hjumpik and Toad Lee are still on the other side, and they were not mentioned.

In a town the Legion holds, under a ship the Toads are assaulting, a guard has ordered them to smile for an execution at which Commander G will preside. One of them has binoculars. One has bought ink and two packs and a candle, and one has a hundred and ten gold and a magnifying glass she did not buy. One has a name for a prosthetist. Nobody has decided what to do next.

WAH.
sections.waluigi_note: Out of the Shadowfell, into a town on the wrong side of a flag. The Legion holds the ship, the Toads are taking it, and the party has binoculars, a rumour and thirty-one gold. Waluigi has attended worse mornings. He cannot name one.

name: The TOADALNAEC and the Three Lies
title: We Are the Toads: A Free Mask, a Gold Handshake, a New Toad Carried Through the Ship, a Speaker Who Would Not Show His Hands, and a Duel Nobody Saw Finished
date: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF — the afternoon after the town shop (estimated; the account carries no clock)
timeWindow: 1 Aethel, 1040 BF, an archive estimate anchored at the end of the account. The party sold the gold bar and left the town in the morning (see The Box at the Cottage Door, 10:00); the walk to the ship, the gate, the hall and the duel are placed in the early afternoon. The account carries no clock of its own, and the hour is the archive's.
location: The town beneath the Legionlance, then the gangway and the hall of the old Vigilance, now the Toads' TOADALNAEC (Material)
status: Filed — the ship is the Toads', Speaker L is in a Toad cell, Rivers is on fire, the hall is walking out, and the duel has not ended
summary: Remi is handed a free mask and walks up the gangway of the old Vigilance with the party's toads, where a gate toad insists the ship is the Toads' TOADALNAEC and sends for Hudston, whom Remi turns gold with a handshake. The toads sing Remi through the ship as the new toad, and Speaker Rivers receives the party in a hall: he has taken over Speaker L's post, Speaker L is in a cell, and the Toads recite the three lies of Archie Miser. Markop demands to see Rivers' hands, casts a truth spell on a crowd, hears a toad say he stole something from Archie, and duels Rivers while the crowd walks out.
description:
Waluigi opens this filing with the shortest line in it, sung by the party's toads on the walk up to the ship: **"We are the toads."** It is the song that took Remi to the front door of [the old Vigilance](#/article/vigilance), and the song that was sung to carry her through the rest of it.

The Legion's ship is not the Legion's anymore. It belongs to the Liberated Toads, or to a Speaker who says it does, and he has taken over a job that the party thought was still held by a toad now in a cell on a lower deck. He has a tea service, a crowd and a lesson plan, and the lesson is that Archie Miser is a liar, a madman and a man who put Toads back in their place. By the end of the afternoon the lesson has been put to a hall of toads, to a barrel, and to a centaur with a spellbook.
outcome: The Toads hold the old Vigilance, which they call the TOADALNAEC, and Speaker Rivers holds the Toads. Speaker L is in a cell. Dan has been told to report to Rivers and not to the Pond Patrol. Archie is in a barrel and Green T has the barrel. Remi has turned a handful of toads gold. Markop has challenged Rivers, forced a look at his hands, cast a truth spell that Rivers refused to acknowledge, set Rivers alight, and is left in a hall whose crowd has started to leave.
notableFeatures: A free mask from a shopkeeper who underpays on everything else
A ship with two names and one layout
A toad who goes gold on a handshake and asks to be shot
A song that carries a recruit through the ship
The three lies of Archie Miser, recited by the people he saved
'Get away from me, you filth animal. Surround her. Oh, oopsie.'
A speaker with his hands in his pockets
A truth spell that worked on the wrong toad
A duel conducted with a pen and a battleaxe

reputationNotes.markop: Called the Toads' command a coup in front of the Toads and asked them whether a speaker who would not show his hands had earned their trust. The crowd was still walking out of the hall when the account ended.
reputationNotes.archie_miser: Named by the Toads in the hall as an arsonist and a liar. The people who hold that view are the ones he says he saved.
reputationNotes._record: Nothing else moved. The Toads' regard for the Legion was not tested, and the ship's new name is the Toads' own.

aftermath:
**The ship is the Toads'.** [the old Vigilance](#/article/vigilance) carries a Toad name, and the gate the party tried to claim was held without a sign of the Legion.

**Speaker Rivers holds the Toads.** He took Speaker L's job, he says, while the party handled the manor, and the party has been told to report to him. Rodger is named; the Pond Patrol is not.

**Speaker L is in a Toad cell.** The Legion arrested him, the Toads say they got him back, and they put him in jail.

**Archie is in a barrel.** Green T has pulled it back. The Toads still hold that he is an arsonist and a liar.

**A toad was silenced mid-sentence.** He said he stole something from Archie and was sent to the dungeon with tea in his mouth.

**The duel is open.** Rivers is burning. Markop is ready for another strike. The hall is leaving.

**The mask is on Remi's sheet.** Nobody has put it on.
waluigiAssessment:
**1. The ship changed hands, and the argument about it never changed.** The gate toad's case was that the layout was the same. The party's case was that the ship was theirs. The archive files the afternoon as two sets of people who both thought they owned the old Vigilance, and the only thing that settled it at the gangway was a song.

**2. The mask is the only thing that was free, and the only thing that was gold.** Remi was handed a mask, refused to wear it, and within the hour was turning Toads gold with a touch. The account puts them in the same afternoon and says nothing connecting them. The archive does the same and wants it on the record that it noticed.

**3. Rivers showed the floor.** He claimed to have killed with his bare hands, was asked for his hands, and held up dirt. The Toads took a metaphor for chains. Whatever he did, the account does not file him in a fight.

**4. The third lie covers the first two.** 'Anything Archie says is a lie' means nobody has to check the other two. A crowd that has been taught that does not need to look at a village.

**5. The truth spell worked, and was stopped with a teapot.** A toad in range said he stole something from Archie. Rivers answered with the tea. The archive is waiting for the dungeon to say what it was.

sections.name: I. For Free
sections.overview:
The gold bar was gone, and the coins it had been turned into were in a pocket, and [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) was in the mood to spend the rest of the afternoon on something other than a shop.

"Now that I sold money to that guy," she said, "we can go on an adventure."

The shopkeeper, the same one who had paid a third of what the bar was worth, came out from behind the counter. "I have an adventure mask for you," he said, "and it's free."

"For free?" Remi said. "It does sound interesting. For free."

He put it in her hands. It was gloomy. She looked at it for as long as it took to decide. "I won't wear it," she said. "Maybe the toads will."

Then she and the others went out of the door. [Green T](#/article/green_t) went after them. "I'd better supervise them," he said.

The toads in the party sang as they walked, and the song was short:

**"We are the toads."**

*WAH! A counter that pays a third gives away a mask. The archive has priced a great many free things and would like it noted that the shop only ever gave anything away after it had finished taking.*
sections.waluigi_note: Nothing in the account says what the mask does, who it was made for, or why a shopkeeper who offers a third on everything lets a gloomy one go for nothing. The archive has the mask on the sheet and has not been told what it is. WAH.

sections.name: II. Whose Airship
sections.overview:
[the old Vigilance](#/article/vigilance) was where they had left it, and the gangway had a toad on it.

"Who goes there?" the toad said.

"Us," said the party. "The owners of the airship."

"That's not right," the toad said.

"What do you mean it's ours?"

"No, no, no, no. This is the TOADS' airship. The TOADALNAEC. It belongs to [Speaker Rivers](#/article/speaker_rivers)."

"No, no, it may be the same layout," came the answer, "but I assure you it's ours."

The toad on the gangway looked at them, and then over his shoulder, and then he made the decision of every gate guard in every archive: he sent for someone else. "Come on out, Hudston," he called. "We have a problem."

*WAH! The Legion renamed this ship and got it wrong. The Toads have renamed it back and got it wronger. TOADALNAEC. Waluigi has said it forty times to himself and has not yet found where the stress goes.*
sections.waluigi_note: The ship on the gangway is the Vigilance. Both sides in the argument say the layout is the same, because it is. Neither side, at any point in the account, says the other is wrong about the layout. Only about whose it is.

sections.name: III. Gold or Gold-Plated
sections.overview:
[Hudston](#/article/hudston) came out on deck and stopped when he saw [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory).

"Wow," he said. "Are you gold, or gold-plated?"

"Come and find out for yourself," said Remi, and she shook his hand.

The gold started at the palm. It ran up his arm and across his shoulders and out to his feet, and when it had stopped he looked at himself for a moment and turned to the gangway.

"Hey, guys," Hudston said. "Check it out. I'm gold now."

"You want to test it out?" Remi asked.

[Green T](#/article/green_t) told him to stand against the wall, and Hudston stood against the wall, and Green T shot him. The bullet rang off the gold and went somewhere else.

"Wow," Hudston said. "How can I ever repay you? It kind of stung, but it's really fun."

Green T shot again, with the same result.

The other toads on the gangway said the sentence the afternoon was about to be built on.

**"You're one of the toads now."**
sections.waluigi_note: The account does not say that the mask caused the gold. It does not say that the mask didn't. It says a girl was handed a thing for free, would not put it on, and was shaking hands with metal within the hour. The archive is not going to settle that and would like the room to stop looking at Waluigi.

sections.name: IV. The New Toad
sections.overview:
Remi started singing. It was not a good song, and she did not stop.

*Oh, I'm the new toad, listen to me, I'll sing a song in the air or the sea,* she sang, and the toads sang it back.

They picked her up. The new toad, the crowd sang, will be **very small, nimble and happy.** "What a fun game," they said. "We will see."

They carried her through the ship, singing, all the way along.

*Oh, I'm a new toad, listen to me, I'll sing you a song, the air and the sea.*

Behind them, the others had worked out what they were looking at. The toads from Disaster Inc. went after Remi to try to save the rest of the party, and caught up with the song in time to see the toads set Remi down.
sections.waluigi_note: Waluigi would like the record to show that nobody sang her a lullaby by accident. The verse is a recruitment drive with a tune, and the tune worked on a girl who had been given a mask for free an hour earlier. It has been a day.

sections.name: V. Speaker Rivers Receives
sections.overview:
[Speaker Rivers](#/article/speaker_rivers) came out into the hall like a man arriving at his own party.

"Oh, good," he said. "New recruits."

The hall was full of toads, and the party was in the middle of them. "You guys with our toads," [Dan](#/article/dan_the_toad) asked, "or...?"

"They're with me," said Speaker Rivers.

He looked at the party for a moment and nodded to himself. "Hmm. I don't know. So you're the Liberated Toads, right?"

"I feel kind of independent," Dan said. "I got back with Rodger. Is anyone here from the Pond Patrol? I have to report to them."

"Oh, don't worry about them," said Rivers. "You report to me now. I took over Speaker L's job while you were handling the whole manor situation."

Then [Archie](#/article/archie_miser) walked into the hall, and everybody saw him.

**"IT'S HIM! THE MAN WHO BREATHES FIRE! ARREST HIM FOR CRIMES AGAINST THE TOADS!"**

"What's going on here?" Archie asked. [Markop](#/article/markop) had already taken a step forward.

"Is this legal?" he asked. "The Legion arrested [Speaker L](#/article/speaker_l)."

"No," said a toad. "We got him back. And we put him in jail."

"Isn't this a coup d'état?" Markop said. "Let me duel you. You're unfit to rule."

"Fine," said Speaker Rivers.

*WAH! Speaker L was arrested by the Legion, rescued by the Toads and put in a Toad cell by the rescuers. That is a single sentence, and everybody in the room said it with a straight face.*
sections.waluigi_note: Rivers took Speaker L's job 'while you guys handled the whole manor situation.' The 'manor situation' is the party's whole last month, and Rivers uses the phrase the way a man uses it who was not at the manor. The archive has no date for when Speaker L's post changed hands and nobody in the hall offered one.

sections.name: VI. The Three Lies
sections.overview:
Markop walked out onto the floor to meet him and dodged a trapdoor on the way. Archie fell into a barrel. The account does not say how.

"I saved you from slavery!" Archie said from inside it.

The toads picked up the barrel. It went up on shoulders. Markop started to argue with them and was told that Archie was an arsonist, and Markop said they had been saved by him, and Archie Miser fell into a barrel, which the account says twice, so the archive does too.

[Gentlepad](#/article/toad_gentlepad) came up to Markop. "Stand still," Gentlepad said, "while we get these Archie germs off of you."

"What have they been telling you?" Archie asked from the barrel.

"The three lies of Archie Miser," the toads told him, and they took him through them one at a time, each with its correction.

**"1. He saved the toads."** "No. He didn't save them. He put them back in their place, to be cogs in the machine."

**"2. Archie Miser is a sane individual."** "False. Archie Miser is INSANE. He burnt down a village full of orphans."

"That ain't true," Archie said. "I do have flaws, but the village never happened. On remembering it was someone else."

**"3. Anything Archie says is a lie."**

"That's it," a toad said. "Those are the three Miserly principles."

"Okay," Markop said, "so if that was true, why isn't he fireballing us right now?"

"Because he's scared of me," said Speaker Rivers.

"Archie fought an evil tree," said Markop.

*WAH! Three lies, recited by toads, ending in the fact that the third one covers the first two. The archive would call it a logical trick if the ship were not holding the logician in a barrel.*
sections.waluigi_note: The second lie is a charge of burning a village of orphans, and Archie answers that the village never happened and that he remembers it being someone else. The archive has nothing to put under either half of that. It files the charge and the reply side by side and declines to pick.

sections.name: VII. Why
sections.overview:
From the barrel, Archie spoke to Rivers, and it was the longest thing he said all day.

"This is the first time I've met you," he said. "You don't scare me at all. If I wanted to, I would do what Markop did. But I'm nice, and so I need to understand why you hate me. I saved you guys, all hundred and fifty of you. So why?"

Nobody in the hall answered it. "Well," Archie said, "take it away, Remi."

[Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) had been listening with her head on one side. "I'm not sure why Archie is evil," she said, "but why not?"

She went for a high five, up high. [Speaker Rivers](#/article/speaker_rivers) dodged it.

"Get away from me, you filth animal!" he said, and then, to the toads, "Surround her. Oh, oopsie."

He had caught himself. It was too late. The whole hall of toads said the same thing together.

**"Huh?"**

"You guys want to be called that?" Markop asked, into the quiet. The toads paused, and the pause went round the hall.

*WAH! A recruiter's slip is the one thing a crowd always hears, and Rivers had just told his own followers what he called them when he thought they weren't listening. Waluigi has been bitten by that dog before.*
sections.waluigi_note: 'All hundred and fifty of you' is Archie's number, given from a barrel. The archive has no other count and files this one as his.

sections.name: VIII. Show Me Your Hands
sections.overview:
Markop turned to the hall.

"Did anyone actually see Speaker Rivers fight?"

"Yeah," Rivers said. "I fought. Killed them with my bare hands." He put his hands in his pockets.

"Let me see your hands," said Markop. "They should be bruised and bloodied."

The hands stayed where they were. "Out of your pockets," Markop said. Rivers made a fake stumble and tripped on the floor, and when he came up he held both hands out.

"See?" he said. "My hands are dirty. Dirt and dust."

"I said bruised and bloodied," said Markop. "See? He's lying to you."

"I personally unchained you guys," said Rivers, "and freed you."

Markop asked the hall whether anyone remembered being unchained by Rivers.

"The metaphorical chains," Rivers said.

"Makes sense," said a toad.

"Wasn't Speaker L the savior?" Markop asked.

"No," said Rivers. "He was a vigilante criminal."

Markop was about to say something, and then he saw [Green T](#/article/green_t) on the far side of the room, pulling the barrel back. He gave him a look. Green T nodded back.

Over by the wall, [Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) spun round to watch. Another toad had turned gold.
sections.waluigi_note: The hands are the whole case. A toad who says he killed with them has to show them, and Rivers was asked for his hands and produced the floor. The chains turned out to be metaphorical, and the Toads took that without a murmur.

sections.name: IX. Tea, and the Truth Spell
sections.overview:
[Speaker Rivers](#/article/speaker_rivers) said he was a bit too tired and asked whether anyone could carry him, and the toads carried him.

"Your tea's ready, sir," one of them said, and he drank it.

"That's not a potion, is it?" Markop asked.

"No, no. Just tea."

Markop looked down at his spellbook and smiled. "We don't have to fight," he said. "You just have to tell the truth, and I'll go. I have a spell that will make it so you can't lie. I ask you questions."

[Remi](#/article/remi_akamatsu_full_backstory) had gotten bored. She leaned on a toad, and the toad went gold. She yawned and hit another, and he went gold. She kicked her legs back, and a third.

The tea came. Rivers sipped.

"Of course," he said, "I'd never lie to anyone."

Markop pointed at him. "Now say the truth spell didn't work."

"Maybe you're a bad magician," said Rivers.

Markop lost his temper. "You want me to beam you?"

"No," Rivers said, quickly.

Markop turned to the toad next to him, who was in range of the spell. "Tell me your secret."

"I like lifting up people," the toad said, "and I also stole something from Archi—"

Rivers forced the tea down the toad's throat, and the toad threw up.

"Hey," said Markop. "What did he steal?"

"Into the dungeon with him," said Speaker Rivers. They dragged the toad away. He drank another one, a blue one this time, a coffee.

*WAH! A speaker accused of lying asked for his tea and then used it to stop another man talking. The account has the whole interrogation in two cups.*
sections.waluigi_note: The toad was inside the spell and the spell did not misfire. It said a true thing, and a second later someone silenced the speaker with the contents of a teapot. Whatever the toad stole from Archie is not on file, because the end of the sentence is a tea cup.

sections.name: X. The Pen and the Axe
sections.overview:
Markop turned back to Rivers. "You're lying. We need to duel. The spell clearly didn't work."

"I am the best," said Speaker Rivers. "It's not a lie."

Archie was still in his barrel.

Rivers attacked Markop with a pen. The pen, he said, is mightier than the sword.

They duelled. Markop attacked and set Rivers on fire, and Rivers screamed. The battleaxe swung and set him on fire again, and he screamed again. Another swing missed. Someone grabbed for the battleaxe and was too weak to take it.

Then the toads began to walk away.

"Lame," some of them said as they went. "He's losing his crowd."

Markop smiled, and got ready for another strike. The account ends there.
sections.waluigi_note: The account never says whose hands the burning battleaxe was in, or which man was too weak to take it. The archive files the hall emptying out as the only clear outcome of the fight. WAH.
